7.1.1.1: Vyāsa said: Salutation to Śiva, to Soma, the one accompanied by Umā, together with his attendants and with his sons, to the Lord of Pradhāna and Puruṣa, the cause of creation, preservation and dissolution. ॥1॥
7.1.1.2: Whose power is incomparable and whose sovereignty is all-pervading; the wise declare lordship and omnipresence to be his very nature. ॥2॥
7.1.1.3: I go for refuge to that unborn one, the maker of the universe, eternal, auspicious, imperishable—Mahādeva, the great-souled Śiva. ॥3॥
7.1.1.4: In the field of dharma, at the great holy ford, the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the Kālindī (Yamunā), at Prayāga, in the Naimiṣa forest, on the path to Brahmā's world— ॥4॥
7.1.1.5: the sages of praiseworthy self, devoted to vows of truth, of great energy and great fortune, performed a great sacrificial session. ॥5॥
7.1.1.6: Having heard there of the sacrificial session of those of unwearied deeds, came the disciple of the wise Vedavyāsa, the very son of Satyavatī— ॥6॥
7.1.1.7: a disciple, great-souled and intelligent, renowned in the three worlds, knowing the merits and faults of a statement endowed with the five members of argument, ॥7॥
7.1.1.8: able to give ever better replies even to Bṛhaspati when he speaks; and of tales sweet to hear, with charming words and sections— ॥8॥
7.1.1.9: a skilled narrator of such tales, knower of time and of right conduct, a poet—that Sūta, best of Purāṇa-reciters, came to that place. ॥9॥
7.1.1.10: Seeing that Sūta arriving, the sages, delighted in mind, offered him kind words and worship in due manner. ॥10॥
7.1.1.11: Accepting that worship offered by the sages, he, being invited, took the seat assigned to him, befitting himself. ॥11॥
7.1.1.12: Then, from that very meeting with him, the minds of the sages of purified selves became eager to hear a Purāṇic tale. ॥12॥
7.1.1.13: Then the great sages, having honoured him with agreeable words and made him well disposed toward them, spoke these words: ॥13॥
7.1.1.14: The sages said: O Romaharṣaṇa, all-knowing one, by the weight of our good fortune you have arrived today, O greatly blessed one, O king among Śaivas, O great-minded one. ॥14॥
7.1.1.15: You obtained the entire lore of the Purāṇas directly from Vyāsa; therefore you are indeed the vessel of wondrous tales, ॥15॥
7.1.1.16: as the ocean is the mine of gems of great worth. Whatever has been, whatever will be, and whatever other thing exists— ॥16॥
7.1.1.17: nothing in the three worlds is unknown to you. By the power of destiny you have come here to see us; you ought not to leave in vain without doing us some good. ॥17॥
7.1.1.18: Therefore, quickly recite to us the Purāṇa, most worthy of hearing, holy, joined with knowledge of true tales, the whole essence of the Vedānta. ॥18॥
7.1.1.19: Thus entreated by the sages, expounders of the Veda, Sūta replied in gentle, reasoned and auspicious words. ॥19॥
7.1.1.20: Sūta said: Honoured and favoured by you, and thus urged, why should I not properly narrate the Purāṇa revered by the seers? ॥20॥
7.1.1.21: Having saluted Mahādeva, the Goddess, Skanda, Vināyaka, Nandin, and likewise Vyāsa, the very son of Satyavatī, ॥21॥
7.1.1.22: I shall tell the supreme, holy Purāṇa, equal to the Veda, an ocean of the knowledge of Śiva, which directly grants the fruits of enjoyment and liberation, ॥22॥
7.1.1.23: adorned with the meanings of the Āgamas joined with word, sense and reasoning, which was told long ago by Vāyu in connection with the Śveta Kalpa. ॥23॥
7.1.1.24: Learn from me as I speak of all the branches of knowledge, the sequence of the Purāṇas, and the origin of that Purāṇa. ॥24॥
7.1.1.25: The six limbs, the four Vedas, Mīmāṃsā, the expanse of Nyāya, Purāṇa and Dharmaśāstra—these are the fourteen branches of knowledge. ॥25॥
7.1.1.26: Āyurveda, Dhanurveda and Gāndharva in sequence, and beyond that Arthaśāstra—thus the branches of knowledge are held to be eighteen. ॥26॥
7.1.1.27: Of these eighteen branches of knowledge, following different paths, the original author and seer is Śūlapāṇi (the trident-bearer) himself—so says scripture. ॥27॥
7.1.1.28: He, the lord of all the worlds, wishing to create the entire universe, first produced Brahmā, the eternal, as his own son. ॥28॥
7.1.1.29: To that firstborn son Brahmā, the womb of the universe, the Lord in the beginning gave these branches of knowledge for the creation of the universe. ॥29॥
7.1.1.30: Then, for preservation, he gave the power of protection to the god Hari, Viṣṇu, his middle son, the protector even of Brahmā. ॥30॥
7.1.1.31: Brahmā the ordainer, having received knowledge and carrying out the creation of beings, first remembered the Purāṇa among all the scriptures. ॥31॥
7.1.1.32: Afterwards the Vedas issued from his mouths; then from his mouth arose the course of all the scriptures. ॥32॥
7.1.1.33: When the people on earth were unable to grasp its vastness, then, to condense the knowledge, by the command of the Lord of the universe, ॥33॥
7.1.1.34: at the end of each Dvāpara age, Viṣṇu, the soul of the universe, its sustainer, the lord, descends onto this earth and moves about under the name Vyāsa. ॥34॥
7.1.1.35: Thus, O twice-born ones, in each Dvāpara the Vedas were divided, and the Purāṇas and other works were composed thereafter. ॥35॥
7.1.1.36: Again, in this Dvāpara, he was born of Satyavatī under the name Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana, as fire is born from the araṇi (fire-stick). ॥36॥
7.1.1.37: That sage, condensing the Vedas again, made them fourfold; and the sage again arranged the condensed lore eighteenfold. Because he divided the Vedas, he is known in the world as Vedavyāsa. ॥37॥
7.1.1.38: And the corpus of the Purāṇas was condensed to the measure of four hundred thousand verses; even today in the world of the gods it extends to a thousand million. ॥38॥
7.1.1.39: A twice-born who knows the four Vedas with their limbs and Upaniṣads, but does not know the Purāṇa, can by no means be called learned. ॥39॥
7.1.1.40: One should amplify the Veda by means of the Itihāsa and Purāṇa. The Veda fears one of little learning, thinking: This one will strike me. ॥40॥
7.1.1.41: Creation, secondary creation, genealogy, the Manu-periods, and the deeds of the dynasties: a Purāṇa has these five characteristics. ॥41॥
7.1.1.42: This Purāṇa is taught as tenfold and as eightfold by the sages, foremost knowers of the truth, according to the distinction of extensive and concise versions. ॥42॥
7.1.1.43: The Brāhma, the Pādma, the Vaiṣṇava, the Śaiva, likewise the Bhāgavata, the Bhaviṣya, the Nāradīya, and after that the Mārkaṇḍeya; ॥43॥
7.1.1.44: The Āgneya, the Brahmavaivarta, the Laiṅga, the Vārāha, the Skānda, the Vāmana, the Kaurma, the Mātsya and the Gāruḍa; ॥44॥
7.1.1.45: And the Brahmāṇḍa: this is the holy sequence of the Purāṇas. Among them the Śaiva, which is the fourth, belongs to Śarva and accomplishes all aims. ॥45॥
7.1.1.46: That text has the extent of a hundred thousand verses, arranged in twelve saṃhitās. It was composed by Śiva himself, and in it dharma is established. ॥46॥
7.1.1.47: By the very dharma declared in it, men of the three twice-born classes are Śaivas. Therefore one seeking liberation should take refuge in Śiva alone. ॥47॥
7.1.1.48: Even for the gods, liberation comes only by taking refuge in him, and not otherwise. ॥48॥
7.1.1.49: This Śaiva Purāṇa, which has been described as equal to the Veda — learn its divisions from me as I state them briefly. ॥49॥
7.1.1.50: The Vidyeśvara, likewise the Raudra, the unsurpassed Vaināyaka, the Auma, the Mātṛ Purāṇa, and likewise the Rudraikādaśaka; ॥50॥
7.1.1.51: The Kailāsa, the Śatarudra, the one called Koṭirudra, the one called Sahasrakoṭirudra, and after that the Vāyavīya; ॥51॥
7.1.1.52: And the Purāṇa called Dharma: thus there are twelve saṃhitās. The Vidyeśa is stated to be ten thousand in verse-count. ॥52॥
7.1.1.53: The Raudra, the Vaināyaka, the Auma, and after that the one called Mātṛkā are each eight thousand; the next is thirteen thousand — ॥53॥
7.1.1.54: namely the one called Rudraikādaśaka; the Kailāsa is six thousand; the Śatarudra three thousand; then the Koṭirudra — ॥54॥
7.1.1.55: is of nine thousand, endowed with knowledge of all matters; the one called Sahasrakoṭirudra is eleven thousand; ॥55॥
7.1.1.56: the unsurpassed Vāyavīya numbers four thousand; and the Purāṇa called Dharma is twelve thousand. ॥56॥
7.1.1.57: Thus the Śaiva Purāṇa is declared to be a hundred thousand verses by the division of its branches. That Purāṇa is the essence of the Veda and bestows the fruits of enjoyment and liberation. ॥57॥
7.1.1.58: But it was abridged by Vyāsa into twenty-four thousand verses. Among the Purāṇas, the Śaiva Purāṇa is indeed the fourth, consisting of seven saṃhitās. ॥58॥
7.1.1.59: Of these the first is called Vidyeśvara, the second the Rudra Saṃhitā, the third called Śatarudra, the fourth Koṭirudra; ॥59॥
7.1.1.60: the fifth is said to be the Umā, the sixth the Kailāsa Saṃhitā, the seventh the one called Vāyavīya: thus there are seven saṃhitās here. ॥60॥
7.1.1.61: The Vidyeśvara is two thousand; the Raudra ten thousand five hundred; the Śatarudra is declared as two thousand plus thirty and one hundred and fifty, that is 2,180; ॥61॥
7.1.1.62: such is the Śatarudra; likewise the Koṭirudra is two thousand two hundred with forty more (sky 0 and yuga 4) added, that is 2,240; and the Auma is one (earth) thousand — ॥62॥
7.1.1.63: with eight hundred and forty, that is 1,840; the Kailāsa is one thousand with two hundred and forty, that is 1,240; after that the Vāyavīya — ॥63॥
7.1.1.64: numbers four thousand. Thus, by the distinction of these numbers, the supremely holy Purāṇa called Śiva has been heard. ॥64॥
7.1.1.65: The Vāyavīya, which is declared to be of four thousand verses — this I shall now narrate, comprising its two parts. ॥65॥
7.1.1.66: This unsurpassed scripture should not be told to one who does not know the Veda, nor to one without faith, nor likewise to one who does not know the Purāṇas. ॥66॥
7.1.1.67: It should be given to a disciple who has been tested, who is righteous and free of envy, a devotee of Śiva who follows Śiva's dharma. ॥67॥
7.1.1.68: Salutation to that blessed Vyāsa of immeasurable splendour, by whose grace the compilation of the Purāṇas abides in me. ॥68॥
7.1.1.iti: Thus ends the first adhyāya, named The account of the descent of knowledge, in the Pūrva-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥1॥
7.1.2.1: Sūta said: Long ago, after a great length of time, when kalpa after kalpa had passed, and when this present kalpa had arrived and the work of creation had begun, ॥1॥
7.1.2.2: when livelihood had been established and the creatures had awakened to understanding, among the sages of the six lineages, speaking with one another, ॥2॥
7.1.2.3: a very great dispute arose: This is the Supreme, This is not. Because the Supreme is hard to determine, no certainty was reached on that matter. ॥3॥
7.1.2.4: They went to see the Ordainer, the imperishable Brahmā, where the blessed Brahmā dwells, praised by gods and asuras, ॥4॥
7.1.2.5: on the auspicious, delightful peak of Meru, crowded with gods and dānavas, thronged with siddhas and cāraṇas, frequented by yakṣas and gandharvas, ॥5॥
7.1.2.6: resounding with flocks of birds, adorned with gems and coral, beautified by bowers, caves, grottoes, dwellings and waterfalls. ॥6॥
7.1.2.7: There is a forest called Brahmavana, full of various animals, ten yojanas wide and a hundred yojanas long, ॥7॥
7.1.2.8: with lovely lakes full of sweet, clear water, and with lovely flowering trees covered by intoxicated bees. ॥8॥
7.1.2.9: There is a beautiful great city, resembling the rising sun, unassailable even for daityas, dānavas and rākṣasas proud of their irresistible strength, ॥9॥
7.1.2.10: made of refined gold, with lofty ramparts and gateways, adorned with hundreds of turrets, balconies, pinnacles and streets, ॥10॥
7.1.2.11: decorated with countless crores of great mansions, variegated with precious gems, as though licking the sky. ॥11॥
7.1.2.12: In it dwells Brahmā, the Prajāpati, together with his assembly. Going there, they saw the great-souled Grandfather of the worlds in person. ॥12॥
7.1.2.13: The sages, godlike, saw him served by hosts of divine seers, shining like pure gold, adorned with all ornaments, ॥13॥
7.1.2.14: with a serene face, gentle, with eyes long like lotus petals, endowed with divine radiance, anointed with divine fragrances, ॥14॥
7.1.2.15: wearing divine white garments, adorned with divine garlands, whose lotus feet are worshipped by the lords of gods, asuras and yogins, ॥15॥
7.1.2.16: shining with Sarasvatī, whose limbs bear all auspicious marks and who holds a fly-whisk in her hand, like the sun with its radiance. ॥16॥
7.1.2.17: Seeing him, all the sages, their faces and eyes brightened, placed joined palms on their heads and praised the foremost of gods. ॥17॥
7.1.2.18: The sages said: Salutation to you of threefold form, the cause of creation, preservation and dissolution; to the ancient Person, to Brahmā, the Supreme Self. ॥18॥
7.1.2.19: Salutation to you whose body is Pradhāna, who agitates Pradhāna, who is transformed in twenty-three categories, yet is himself unchanging. ॥19॥
7.1.2.20: Salutation to you whose body is the cosmic egg, who dwells within the cosmic egg, whose works there are accomplished and whose instruments are perfect. ॥20॥
7.1.2.21: Salutation to you who are all the worlds, the maker of all worlds, the cause that ordains the union and separation of all selves with bodies. ॥21॥
7.1.2.22: By you alone the whole world is created, withdrawn and protected; yet, because of māyā, O Lord, O Grandfather, we do not know you. ॥22॥
7.1.2.23: Sūta said: Thus praised by the highly fortunate great seers, Brahmā spoke in a deep voice, as if gladdening the sages. ॥23॥
7.1.2.24: Brahmā said: O seers, highly fortunate, of great goodness and great vigour, for what purpose have you all come here together? ॥24॥
7.1.2.25: To the god Brahmā, who spoke thus, all those foremost knowers of Brahman, with joined palms, spoke in words full of humility. ॥25॥
7.1.2.26: The sages said: O Lord, we are enveloped by a great darkness; wearied and disputing, we do not see here what is the Supreme. ॥26॥
7.1.2.27: For you are the sustainer of the whole world, the cause of all causes; indeed, O Lord, nothing here exists that is unknown to you. ॥27॥
7.1.2.28: Who is the Being beyond all beings, the ancient, supreme Person, utterly pure, perfectly full, eternal, the Supreme Lord? ॥28॥
7.1.2.29: By whom, through wondrous action, is the world first created? Tell us the truth, O greatly wise one, to remove our doubt. ॥29॥
7.1.2.30: Thus asked, Brahmā, his eyes widened and smiling in wonder, in the presence of gods, dānavas and sages, ॥30॥
7.1.2.31: rose, meditated for a long while, and uttering the word Rudra, his whole body moist with bliss, spoke with joined palms. ॥31॥
7.1.2.iti: Thus ends the second adhyāya, named The description of the sages' proposal, in the Pūrva-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥2॥
7.1.3.1: Brahmā said: He is the one from whom words turn back together with the mind, not having reached him; the wise one who knows his bliss fears nothing from any quarter. ॥1॥
7.1.3.2: From whom this whole universe, beginning with Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra and Indra, together with all the elements and senses, is first brought forth; ॥2॥
7.1.3.3: Who is the ordainer of all causes, the one to be meditated upon, the supreme cause, and who is never born from anything else, from anywhere, at any time; ॥3॥
7.1.3.4: Endowed with all sovereignty, himself called by name Sarveśvara (Lord of all), Śambhu, abiding in the midst of the heart's space, is to be meditated upon by all who seek liberation. ॥4॥
7.1.3.5: Who in the beginning created me as his son and imparts knowledge to me; by his grace I have obtained this position of Prajāpati. ॥5॥
7.1.3.6: The Lord who, alone, stands in heaven, motionless like a tree; the great-souled Person by whom this whole universe is filled; ॥6॥
7.1.3.7: The one active among the many inactive beings, who alone makes the one seed manifold — he is Maheśvara. ॥7॥
7.1.3.8: The Lord who, through these souls, rules all these worlds; who is the one blessed Rudra — there is no second whatsoever. ॥8॥
7.1.3.9: Who, though always seated in the hearts of people, is imperceptible to others; perceiving the universe, he presides over it at all times. ॥9॥
7.1.3.10: Who, the one Lord of infinite power, presides over all the causes, even those free from time; ॥10॥
7.1.3.11: For whom there is neither day nor night, none equal and none greater; whose supreme power is innate and eternal, as are his knowledge and action. ॥11॥
7.1.3.12: This perishable unmanifest matter, and that which is the immortal imperishable soul — over both of these, the perishable and the imperishable, the one god Hara himself rules. ॥12॥
7.1.3.13: rules. Through meditation on him, through union with him and contemplation of reality, the cosmic māyā of this bound soul finally ceases altogether. ॥13॥
7.1.3.14: In whom neither lightning shines, nor the sun, nor the moon; by whose light this world shines — such is the eternal Śruti. ॥14॥
7.1.3.15: The one god, Mahādeva, is to be known as Maheśvara; no state higher than him is attained. ॥15॥
7.1.3.16: He is the first, without beginning or end, pure by his very nature, independent and wholly complete; the moving and unmoving world is subject to his own will. ॥16॥
7.1.3.17: His body is not of prakṛti; he is glorious, beyond the perceived and its marks; he is free and the liberator, timeless, yet the impeller of time. ॥17॥
7.1.3.18: His abode is above all, he is the abode of all, all-knowing, the lord of this entire world made of the sixfold path (adhvan). ॥18॥
7.1.3.19: He is higher than all successively higher beings, with none higher than himself; he is the bee delighting in the nectar of the endless, infinite mass of bliss. ॥19॥
7.1.3.20: He is skilled at gathering together the unbroken cosmic eggs of the worlds; he is an ocean of generosity, valour, depth and sweetness. ॥20॥
7.1.3.21: There is no thing equal to him, nor anything greater; incomparable, he stands as the king of kings of all beings. ॥21॥
7.1.3.22: By him, the doer of wonders, the world is first created; and at the time of the end it will again go to dissolution in him. ॥22॥
7.1.3.23: All beings are under his control; he is the director of all. But he is seen through supreme devotion, and never otherwise. ॥23॥
7.1.3.24: Vows, all kinds of gifts, austerities and observances were declared of old by the good for the sake of cultivating this devotion — of this there is no doubt. ॥24॥
7.1.3.25: Hari, I, Rudra, and likewise the other gods and demons, even today long to see him through fierce austerities. ॥25॥
7.1.3.26: He is invisible to the fallen, the deluded and the wicked and contemptible; but by devotees he is to be worshipped inwardly and outwardly, and even conversed with. ॥26॥
7.1.3.27: His form is threefold: gross, subtle, and beyond that. The gross is visible to immortals such as us, the subtle to yogins; ॥27॥
7.1.3.28: but that which is beyond — eternal, knowledge, bliss, imperishable — is visible to devotees established in it, devoted to it, who have taken up its vow. ॥28॥
7.1.3.29: What use is saying much here? Devotion to Śiva is the supreme secret, more secret than the secret; there is no doubt — one endowed with it is liberated. ॥29॥
7.1.3.30: That devotion comes from grace alone, and grace arises from devotion — just as the seed comes from the sprout, or the sprout from the seed. ॥30॥
7.1.3.31: All attainments of the bound soul everywhere are preceded by grace alone; and that grace is in the end accomplished by all the means of practice. ॥31॥
7.1.3.32: The means to grace is dharma, and it is shown by the Veda. Through its repeated practice comes an equalization of one's former merit and sin. ॥32॥
7.1.3.33: From this balance comes contact with grace, then an increase of dharma; having attained an abundance of dharma, the bound soul's sin is destroyed. ॥33॥
7.1.3.34: Thus, for one whose sins have been gradually destroyed through many births, devotion preceded by knowledge arises towards the Lord of all, together with Ambā (Sāmba). ॥34॥
7.1.3.35: In accordance with one's devotion, the Lord's grace increases. Through grace comes renunciation of action — with respect to its fruit, not in its own form. ॥35॥
7.1.3.36: Therefore from relinquishing the fruit of action comes auspicious connection with Śiva-dharma; and it is twofold: independent of a guru, and dependent on him. ॥36॥
7.1.3.37: Of these, the dependent one is principal, a hundred times superior to the independent. From this connection with Śiva-dharma comes association with knowledge of Śiva. ॥37॥
7.1.3.38: Through association with knowledge a person sees the faults in saṃsāra; from that comes detachment from sense-objects, and from detachment, the cultivation of devotion. ॥38॥
7.1.3.39: For one who has attained perfection in devotion, steadfastness lies in meditation, not in ritual action; for the person engaged in knowledge and meditation, yoga begins. ॥39॥
7.1.3.40: Through yoga comes supreme devotion, and after that grace; through grace a being is liberated, and the liberated one becomes equal to Śiva. ॥40॥
7.1.3.41: This sequence in the modes of grace is not meant as a fixed rule: whatever the fitness of a person, such is the grace bestowed on him. ॥41॥
7.1.3.42: One is liberated while still in the womb, another likewise while being born; yet another is liberated as a child, as a youth, or as an old man. ॥42॥
7.1.3.43: One who has gone into an animal womb is liberated; another, a dweller in hell; yet another, having attained a high station, is liberated when his own station comes to an end. ॥43॥
7.1.3.44: One, his station exhausted, returns again and is then liberated; another, having entered the path, is liberated after halting again and again along it. ॥44॥
7.1.3.45: Therefore liberation of men is not held to be of a single kind; release comes only through Śiva's grace, in accordance with one's knowledge and disposition. ॥45॥
7.1.3.46: Therefore, to win his grace, free from faults of speech and mind, meditating on Śiva alone, together with your wives, sons and sacred fires, ॥46॥
7.1.3.47: all of you devoted to him, intent on him, united with him, taking refuge in him, performing all rites while gone to him alone in mind, ॥47॥
7.1.3.48: you shall perform a long sacrificial session undertaken for a thousand divine years; at the end of the session Vāyu will come there through the power of the mantras. ॥48॥
7.1.3.49: He himself will tell you what is your highest good, together with the means to it. Then the holy, supremely beautiful city of Vārāṇasī ॥49॥
7.1.3.50: is to be visited, where the glorious Lord of the universe, bearer of the Pināka, ever sports together with the Goddess for the sake of showing grace to his devotees. ॥50॥
7.1.3.51: Having seen a great wonder there, you will come to me; then, O best of the twice-born, I shall tell you the means to liberation, ॥51॥
7.1.3.52: by which, in a single birth, liberation will lie in the palm of your hand — liberation that brings release from the bondage of saṃsāra through many births. ॥52॥
7.1.3.53: This mind-made wheel created by me is being released; where its rim wears away, that place is auspicious for austerity. ॥53॥
7.1.3.54: Having said this, the Grandfather (Brahmā) looked at the mind-made wheel, radiant like the sun, bowed to Mahādeva, and released it. ॥54॥
7.1.3.55: Those Brahmins too, greatly delighted, bowed to the Lord of the worlds and set out toward the place where the rim of that wheel wore away. ॥55॥
7.1.3.56: That wheel, too, its rim worn down, fell upon a smooth, lovely rocky surface in a certain forest with clear, sweet water. ॥56॥
7.1.3.57: For that reason that forest became famous as Naimiṣa, honoured by sages, thronged with many Yakṣas, Gandharvas and Vidyādharas. ॥57॥
7.1.3.58: There Purūravas, who was enjoying the eighteen islands of the ocean, having fallen under the sway of Urvaśī's charms and being driven by fate, ॥58॥
7.1.3.59: wrongfully carried off, out of delusion, the golden sacrificial enclosure; there he was struck down by the enraged sages with thunderbolt-like kuśa grass. ॥59॥
7.1.3.60: Where, of old, the creators of the universe, knowers of Brahman, keeping the gārhapatya fire, wishing to create the world, began a divine sacrificial session; ॥60॥
7.1.3.61: where the rite was performed by learned sages, skilled in grammar, semantics and logic, endowed with power, wisdom and ritual practice; ॥61॥
7.1.3.62: where knowers of the Veda, masters of debate, constantly strike down with their words, by the force of argument and disputation, those who stand outside the doctrine of the Veda; ॥62॥
7.1.3.63: That Naimiṣa was fit for the austerities of the sages — delightful with clear, nectar-like water flowing from rocks born at the foot of crystal mountains, abounding in trees with exceedingly sweet fruit, and free of fierce beasts. ॥63॥
7.1.3.iti: Thus ends the third adhyāya, named The account of Naimiṣa, in the Pūrva-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥3॥
7.1.4.1: Sūta said: In that region the highly fortunate sages, whose vows were praiseworthy, then began a sacrificial session (satra), worshipping Mahādeva. ॥1॥
7.1.4.2: And that sacrificial session of the great sages proceeded, wondrous in every respect, like that of the world-creators of old who wished to create the universe. ॥2॥
7.1.4.3: Then, when time had passed and the session, abounding in sacrificial fees, was completed, Vāyu himself came there at the command of the Grandfather Brahmā. ॥3॥
7.1.4.4: He is the god, disciple of the Self-born Brahmā, who sees all things directly and is self-controlled, under whose command stand the Maruts in seven groups of seven; ॥4॥
7.1.4.5: who, constantly moving the limbs through his own functions beginning with prāṇa, upholds the bodies of all beings; ॥5॥
7.1.4.6: who is endowed with the eight powers beginning with aṇimā (minuteness), and who, moving transversely, sustains the worlds by pure means such as his hands; ॥6॥
7.1.4.7: whom the knowers of the principles (tattva) declare to be born from space (ākāśa), possessing two qualities owing to the combination of touch and sound, and the source of the fiery elements. ॥7॥
7.1.4.8: Seeing him arrived at the hermitage, the sages engaged in the long session, remembering the words of the Grandfather, attained incomparable joy. ॥8॥
7.1.4.9: Then all of them rose, bowed to the one born of space, and arranged a golden seat for him. ॥9॥
7.1.4.10: He too, seated there and duly honoured by the sages, greeted them all in return and then asked about their welfare. ॥10॥
7.1.4.11: Vāyu said: O brahmins, is all well with you here, now that the great sacrifice is finished? I hope the Daityas, destroyers of sacrifice and enemies of the gods, did not trouble you? ॥11॥
7.1.4.12: I hope no expiation or faulty offering arose? I hope the rite was well performed by you, having worshipped the gods with hymns, mantras and recitations, and the ancestors with ancestral rites? ॥12॥
7.1.4.13: I hope that, having worshipped them, the rite was well carried out by you? And now that the great session is over, what do you wish to do next? ॥13॥
7.1.4.14: Thus addressed by Vāyu, devoted to Śiva, all the sages, purified and joyful in mind, replied with humility. ॥14॥
7.1.4.15: The sages said: Today all is well with us; today our austerity has borne good fruit, since you have come here for the increase of our welfare. ॥15॥
7.1.4.16: And hear this past event: formerly, our minds overwhelmed by darkness, we worshipped Prajāpati for the sake of knowledge. ॥16॥
7.1.4.17: He, the refuge of all, graciously said to us who had sought refuge: O brahmins, Rudra is superior to all, the supreme cause. ॥17॥
7.1.4.18: Only one who has devotion sees him, the inconceivable, as he truly is; and devotion comes by his grace, and from grace alone comes liberation (nirvṛti). ॥18॥
7.1.4.19: Therefore, to win his grace, worship Rudra, the supreme cause, in Naimiṣa by means of a long sacrificial session. ॥19॥
7.1.4.20: By his grace, at the end of the session, Vāyu will come there; from his mouth you will gain knowledge, and then welfare will be yours. ॥20॥
7.1.4.21: Having instructed us thus, the Supreme One (Parameṣṭhin) sent us all to this region, O highly fortunate one, longing for your coming. ॥21॥
7.1.4.22: We have been engaged in the long session for a thousand divine years; hence there is nothing else for us to pray for other than your coming. ॥22॥
7.1.4.23: Having heard this past account of the sages engaged in the long session, Vāyu, pleased at heart, sat there surrounded by the sages. ॥23॥
7.1.4.24: Then, asked by those sages, the mighty one, to increase their devotion, briefly described Śarva's (Śiva's) lordly glory, beginning with creation. ॥24॥
7.1.4.iti: Thus ends the fourth adhyāya, named The coming of Vāyu, in the Pūrva-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥4॥
7.1.5.1: Sūta said: There, first, the greatly fortunate dwellers of the Naimiṣa forest, having bowed down in due manner, questioned the lord Pavana (Vāyu). ॥1॥
7.1.5.2: The sages of Naimiṣa said: How did you obtain the knowledge whose object is the Lord? And how did you come to be a disciple of Brahmā, who was born from the Unmanifest? ॥2॥
7.1.5.3: Vāyu said: The nineteenth kalpa should be known as Śvetalohita. In that kalpa the four-faced one Brahmā, desiring to create, performed austerity. ॥3॥
7.1.5.4: Pleased by that intense austerity, his father himself, the best of those possessing form, assuming a divine youthful form — ॥4॥
7.1.5.5: — becoming a sage named Śveta and uttering divine speech, Maheśvara, the god of gods, granted him a vision of himself. ॥5॥
7.1.5.6: Having seen him, his father, the overlord of Brahman and the Lord, Brahmā bowed and obtained the supreme knowledge together with the Gāyatrī. ॥6॥
7.1.5.7: Then he, the four-faced maker of the universe, having obtained this knowledge, created all beings, the stationary and the moving. ॥7॥
7.1.5.8: Since this nectar of knowledge was obtained by Brahmā through hearing it from the Supreme Lord, I in turn obtained it from his very mouth through the power of austerity. ॥8॥
7.1.5.9: The sages said: What is that auspicious knowledge you obtained, truer than the true, by establishing supreme steadfastness in which a person attains happiness? ॥9॥
7.1.5.10: Vāyu said: The knowledge of paśu, pāśa and pati that I obtained long ago — in that a person seeking happiness should place supreme steadfastness. ॥10॥
7.1.5.11: Suffering, born of ignorance, is removed by knowledge alone. Knowledge is the discernment of reality, and reality is held to be threefold. ॥11॥
7.1.5.12: The sentient, the insentient, and the controller of both — this triad is called, in order, paśu, pāśa and pati. ॥12॥
7.1.5.13: The imperishable, the perishable, and what is beyond both perishable and imperishable — this triad is generally so described by the knowers of reality. ॥13॥
7.1.5.14: The imperishable is said to be paśu; the perishable is declared to be pāśa; that which is beyond the perishable and imperishable is called pati. ॥14॥
7.1.5.15: The sages said: What is that which is called perishable, and what is declared imperishable? And what is supreme over the two? Tell us this, O Māruta. ॥15॥
7.1.5.16: Vāyu said: Prakṛti is called the perishable; puruṣa is called the imperishable. Another impels these two — he is the Supreme, the highest Lord. ॥16॥
7.1.5.17: The sages said: What is this that is called prakṛti? Who is this considered puruṣa? By what is there a connection between these two? And who is this impelling Lord? ॥17॥
7.1.5.18: Vāyu said: Prakṛti is declared to be Māyā; puruṣa is the one veiled by Māyā; the connection is through mala and karma; Śiva is the impelling Lord. ॥18॥
7.1.5.19: The sages said: What is this that is called Māyā? Of what nature is the one veiled by Māyā? Of what kind is mala, and whence does it come to him? What is Śivahood, and whence is one Śiva? ॥19॥
7.1.5.20: Vāyu said: Māyā is the power of Maheśvara; the one veiled by Māyā is of the nature of consciousness; mala is the innate veiler of consciousness; Śivahood is purity by its own nature. ॥20॥
7.1.5.21: The sages said: How does Māyā veil the all-pervading soul, and by what cause? For what purpose is the soul veiled, and by what is the veil removed? ॥21॥
7.1.5.22: Vāyu said: Veiling is possible even of the all-pervading, since kalā and the rest are also pervasive. The cause is karma itself, for the sake of experience; the veiling ceases with the destruction of mala. ॥22॥
7.1.5.23: The sages said: What is it that is called kalā and the rest? And what is declared to be karma? What is its beginning, what its end, what its fruit, and what its substratum? ॥23॥
7.1.5.24: For whom is experience, what is to be experienced, and what is the means of that experience? What is the cause of the destruction of mala, and what is the soul like when its mala is destroyed? ॥24॥
7.1.5.25: Vāyu said: Kalā, vidyā, rāga, kāla and niyati are called kalā and the rest. The one who is the experiencer is the puruṣa. ॥25॥
7.1.5.26: Karma is that which consists of merit and demerit and yields pleasure and pain as its fruit; it is beginningless, ends with the experience that exhausts mala, and rests in the ignorant self. ॥26॥
7.1.5.27: Experience is for the destruction of karma; the object of experience is called the Unmanifest; the body, with the external and internal organs as its doors, is the means of experience. ॥27॥
7.1.5.28: Mala is destroyed through grace obtained by intensity of devotion; and when that mala of the self is destroyed, the soul becomes equal to Śiva. ॥28॥
7.1.5.29: The sages said: What is said to be the separate function of each of the five principles, kalā and the rest, by which the self is designated as experiencer and as puruṣa? ॥29॥
7.1.5.30: Of what nature is that Unmanifest, and in what form is it experienced? What is its support in experience, and what is called the body? ॥30॥
7.1.5.31: Vāyu said: Vidyā and kalā reveal the powers of knowing and acting; rāga is the impeller; kāla is the delimiter there; and niyati is the regulator. ॥31॥
7.1.5.32: The Unmanifest is the cause, the origin and dissolution of the three guṇas, which the thinkers on reality call pradhāna and prakṛti. ॥32॥
7.1.5.33: That, whose mark is non-manifestation, becomes manifest through kalā; consisting of pleasure, pain and delusion and possessed of the guṇas, it is experienced in three ways. ॥33॥
7.1.5.34: Sattva, rajas and tamas — these guṇas arise from prakṛti; they abide in prakṛti in subtle form, like oil in sesame seed. ॥34॥
7.1.5.35: Pleasure and the cause of pleasure are, in brief, held to be sāttvika; the rājasa is the opposite of that; while inertia and delusion are tāmasa. ॥35॥
7.1.5.36: The sāttvika is declared to be upward movement; the tāmasa is downward movement; and the middle course is said to be rājasa. ॥36॥
7.1.5.37: The five subtle elements, the five gross elements, the five organs of knowledge and the five organs of action, ॥37॥
7.1.5.38: and the tetrad of pradhāna, buddhi, ahaṅkāra and manas — thus, in brief, the Unmanifest together with its modifications has been described. ॥38॥
7.1.5.39: That which is in the causal state is called the Unmanifest; the manifest is that which has reached the state of effect, like the body and the like, or a pot and the like. ॥39॥
7.1.5.40: Just as an effect such as a pot is not wholly different from clay and the like, so the manifest, such as the body, is not wholly different from the Unmanifest. ॥40॥
7.1.5.41: Therefore the Unmanifest alone is the cause, and it alone is the instruments, the body that is their support, and also what is enjoyed through them; there is nothing else. ॥41॥
7.1.5.42: The sages said: How can there truly exist something distinct from the intellect, the senses and the body, which is denoted by the word self? ॥42॥
7.1.5.43: Vāyu said: The distinctness of the all-pervading Self from intellect, senses and body is certain; some Self surely exists, but the reasoning for it is very hard to grasp. ॥43॥
7.1.5.44: The wise do not accept that intellect, senses or body are the Self, because of memory, because their cognition is not fixed, and because awareness does not pervade the whole body. ॥44॥
7.1.5.45: Hence the one who remembers what was experienced, whose range covers all that is knowable, is sung in the Vedas and Vedāntas as the Inner Controller. ॥45॥
7.1.5.46: Everything is in him, and he, eternal, abides pervading everywhere; yet nowhere and by no one is he seen manifestly. ॥46॥
7.1.5.47: He cannot be grasped by the eye, nor by the other senses; the great Self is ascertained only by the illumined mind. ॥47॥
7.1.5.48: He is neither woman nor man, nor indeed neuter; he is not above, not across, not below, nor anywhere at all. ॥48॥
7.1.5.49: The steadfast man, through inward reflection, always sees him as bodiless within bodies, immovable and imperishable amid moving things. ॥49॥
7.1.5.50: What need of saying much here? The Person is separate from the body; those who see him as not separate have an incorrect vision. ॥50॥
7.1.5.51: Beyond this which is called the body of the Person, there exists nothing more impure, uncontrollable, painful and impermanent. ॥51॥
7.1.5.52: Joined with that body, which is the seed of calamities, the Person becomes happy, miserable and deluded through his own karma. ॥52॥
7.1.5.53: Just as a field flooded with water produces a sprout, so karma flooded by ignorance produces a body. ॥53॥
7.1.5.54: His bodies, future and past, by the thousands, are declared to be abodes of utter unhappiness and certain to end in death. ॥54॥
7.1.5.55: As the embodied one comes again and again into bodies that waste away, a lasting dwelling is never found anywhere by anyone. ॥55॥
7.1.5.56: In these bodies he appears now covered, now freed, by bodies, like the moon's disc in the sky by drifting masses of clouds. ॥56॥
7.1.5.57: Here the Self's condition appears divided by the variety of many bodies, like the marks of dice cast upon a gaming board. ॥57॥
7.1.5.58: No one will ever be his, nor is he anyone's; this association with wife, sons and kinsmen is merely a meeting on the road. ॥58॥
7.1.5.59: Just as one piece of wood and another may meet in the great ocean and, having met, drift apart, so is the meeting of beings. ॥59॥
7.1.5.60: He sees the body, but that body does not see him; some Supreme One sees both of them, yet the two do not see him. ॥60॥
7.1.5.61: Beings from Brahmā down to immobile things are declared to be paśus (bound souls); this illustration is stated for all paśus alike. ॥61॥
7.1.5.62: This paśu, who consumes pleasure and pain, is bound by fetters (pāśas); the wise say he is the instrument of the Lord's play. ॥62॥
7.1.5.63: This ignorant creature has no control over his own pleasure and pain; impelled by the Lord, he would go either to heaven or to the abyss. ॥63॥
7.1.5.64: Sūta said: Having heard these words of Vāyu, the sages, delighted in mind, bowed to that Vāyu, expert in the Śaiva Āgamas, and spoke. ॥64॥
7.1.5.iti: Thus ends the fifth adhyāya, named The description of the knowledge of the principle of Śiva, in the Pūrva-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥5॥
7.1.6.1: The sages said: This one who has been called the bound soul (paśu), and that which has been described as the bond (pāśa): who is this lord of the two, someone distinct from both of them? ॥1॥
7.1.6.2: Vāyu said: There is someone, the abode of endless delightful qualities, the Lord (pati), the maker of the universe, who releases the bound soul from its bond. ॥2॥
7.1.6.3: Without him, how could this creation of the universe come about, since these two, the soul and the bond, are insentient and ignorant? ॥3॥
7.1.6.4: Whatever is insentient, beginning with primordial nature (pradhāna) and atoms, is never seen to be an agent by itself without an intelligent cause. ॥4॥
7.1.6.5: And the world depends on a maker, since it is an effect possessing parts. Therefore agency for the effect belongs to the Lord, not to the soul and the bond. ॥5॥
7.1.6.6: Even the soul's agency is preceded by the Lord's impulsion; its knowledge of how to act is not accurate, like the walking of a blind man. ॥6॥
7.1.6.7: Having understood the self as distinct, and the Impeller as distinct from it, he, then favoured by him, becomes fit for immortality. ॥7॥
7.1.6.8: Beyond the soul, the bond and the Lord there is, in truth, a supreme state. The knower of Brahman, having known that alone, will be freed from the womb of rebirth. ॥8॥
7.1.6.9: The Lord, the liberator of all, supports this combined pair, the perishable and the imperishable, the manifest and the unmanifest: the universe. ॥9॥
7.1.6.10: The enjoyer, the enjoyed and the Impeller: what is to be contemplated is declared to be threefold. For those who know, nothing at all beyond this is to be known. ॥10॥
7.1.6.11: As oil is in sesame seeds, or ghee placed in curd, as water pervades a stream, as fire is in the fire-stick (araṇī), ॥11॥
7.1.6.12: just so the one who is ever disciplined beholds, through truth and austerity, the great Self within the self, distinct from the self. ॥12॥
7.1.6.13: The one Lord who wields the net, having made all these worlds by his own ruling powers, he alone rules. ॥13॥
7.1.6.14: Rudra is always one alone; there is no second whatever. He, having created all the worlds, is their protector, and he withdrew them at the end. ॥14॥
7.1.6.15: He has eyes everywhere, and he has faces everywhere; likewise he has arms everywhere and is endowed with feet everywhere. ॥15॥
7.1.6.16: The one God Maheśvara, generating heaven and earth, he alone is the origin and source of all the gods. ॥16॥
7.1.6.17: He generated Hiraṇyagarbha, the first of the gods. Rudra, the great seer, is greater than all: so declares scripture. ॥17॥
7.1.6.18: I know this great Person, immortal, constant, sun-coloured, the Lord established beyond darkness. ॥18॥
7.1.6.19: There is nothing higher than him, nothing other than the supreme Self; there is nothing smaller, nor greater. By him this world is filled. ॥19॥
7.1.6.20: Having all faces, heads and necks, dwelling in the cave of the heart of all beings, the Blessed One is all-pervading; therefore Śiva is omnipresent. ॥20॥
7.1.6.21: He has hands and feet everywhere, eyes, heads and faces everywhere, ears everywhere; in the world he stands enveloping all. ॥21॥
7.1.6.22: Shining through the functions of all the senses, yet devoid of all senses, he is the master and ruler of all, the refuge and friend of all. ॥22॥
7.1.6.23: He who sees though eyeless, who hears though earless, who knows all, yet of whom there is no knower: him they call the supreme Person. ॥23॥
7.1.6.24: Subtler than the subtle, greater than the great, this imperishable Maheśvara is set in the cave of the heart of this creature. ॥24॥
7.1.6.25: By the grace of the Ordainer, one freed from sorrow beholds that Lord, who is free of desire yet the very embodiment of sacrifice, endowed with surpassing greatness. ॥25॥
7.1.6.26: I know him, unageing, ancient, all-pervading, mighty, of whom the expounders of Brahman declare the absence of birth. ॥26॥
7.1.6.27: Though one, Maheśvara fashions these three worlds in many ways through union with his power, and at the end he withdraws the universe which he brought forth in the beginning. ॥27॥
7.1.6.28: Śiva's supreme power, of wondrous form, is called Sustainer of the universe and Ajā (the unborn). That one unborn female, red, white and black, mother of offspring, one unborn soul... ॥28॥
7.1.6.29: ...lies beside her, the genetrix, delighting in her who bears form; but another unborn one abandons that same Ajā, whose enjoyments have been enjoyed. ॥29॥
7.1.6.30: Two birds, companions joined together, are perched on the same tree. One eats the sweet pippala fruit; the other, not eating, looks on. ॥30॥
7.1.6.31: On this tree the person, sunk and bewildered, grieves. When he sees the other, the Lord, the supreme cause, who is worshipped, ॥31॥
7.1.6.32: and his greatness, then, freed from sorrow, he becomes happy. The Vedic metres, sacrifices, rites, what has been and what is to be, ॥32॥
7.1.6.33: all this universe the master of māyā creates; the other the soul is lodged in it through māyā. Know māyā to be Prakṛti, and the master of māyā to be Maheśvara. ॥33॥
7.1.6.34: By her parts alone this whole world is pervaded. The Lord, subtler than the subtlest, dwelling even in the midst of chaos, ॥34॥
7.1.6.35: the creator of the universe and the one who sets it in motion: knowing Śiva alone as the Lord, one attains supreme peace. ॥35॥
7.1.6.36: He alone is Time, the protector, the overlord and master of the universe. Knowing him, the overlord of the universe, one is released from the noose of death. ॥36॥
7.1.6.37: Knowing the Lord as subtle, like the cream finer than ghee, abiding hidden in all beings, one is freed from all sins. ॥37॥
7.1.6.38: This very one is the supreme God, Maheśvara, the maker of all. Knowing him as seated in the heart, one attains immortality. ॥38॥
7.1.6.39: When all was neither day nor night, neither being nor non-being, Śiva alone, the One, existed, from whom the ancient wisdom came forth. ॥39॥
7.1.6.40: No one has grasped him above, nor across, nor in the middle. There is no likeness of him whose name is Great Glory. ॥40॥
7.1.6.41: Knowing this one alone as unborn, those who fear birth resort to the southern (gracious) face of this Rudra for protection. ॥41॥
7.1.6.42: In the imperishable, infinite, supreme Brahman two principles are declared, named knowledge and ignorance, in which they lie placed as though hidden. ॥42॥
7.1.6.43: The perishable is ignorance, and the immortal is proclaimed as knowledge; but he who rules over both is indeed another — Maheśvara. ॥43॥
7.1.6.44: He who, spreading out each net in many ways and gathering it as one, the mighty one, having created all, exercises sovereignty over all — ॥44॥
7.1.6.45: Illuminating the directions above, below and across, he shines by himself; he who, the one most worthy of choice, presides even over what is devoid of its own nature. ॥45॥
7.1.6.46: Transforming their own nature, all the expressions and the expressed, and the guṇas into the state of the enjoyed and the enjoyer, he presides over that universe. ॥46॥
7.1.6.47: Him indeed, hidden in the secret Upaniṣads, the Brahman higher than the highest, the source of Brahmā, prior to the world, the gods and great sages know. ॥47॥
7.1.6.48: Those who know the god Śiva — grasped by inner devotion, called the desireless, maker of being and non-being, creator of the kalās — abandon the body. ॥48॥
7.1.6.49: Some, deluded, consider the cause to be inherent nature, others time; but this is the greatness of the god, by which this world is made to revolve. ॥49॥
7.1.6.50: By whom this is ever enveloped, since he is the Self that is the time of time — impelled by him, this action unfolds together with the elements. ॥50॥
7.1.6.51: Having performed that action again and again and withdrawn it again and again, and having brought about the union of principle with being, ॥51॥
7.1.6.52: with eight, with three, with two, or again with one, and with time and the qualities of the self, he himself pervades the whole world. ॥52॥
7.1.6.53: Having begun actions with the guṇas, he would join them with inherent nature and the rest; in their absence there would be destruction even of action already done. ॥53॥
7.1.6.54: When karma is exhausted, he then goes on, being in truth other than it. He himself is the origin, the cause of the union of enjoyer and enjoyment. ॥54॥
7.1.6.55: Beyond the three times, partless, he alone is the Supreme Lord, all-knowing, master of the three guṇas, Brahman itself, higher than the highest. ॥55॥
7.1.6.56: Him, of universal form, unborn, Bhava, praiseworthy, lord of creatures, god of gods, worshipped by the world, abiding in our own mind, we worship. ॥56॥
7.1.6.57: He who is beyond time and the rest, from whom this manifold world revolves — the bringer of dharma, remover of sin, lord of enjoyments, and abode of the universe — ॥57॥
7.1.6.58: Him, the supreme great Lord of lords, the supreme deity of deities, the supreme master of masters, beyond the beyond — may we know him, the god, the lord of the lords of the worlds. ॥58॥
7.1.6.59: He has no effect to produce and no cause; none equal to him or greater is seen anywhere in the world. ॥59॥
7.1.6.60: His supreme power is heard in scripture to be manifold and innate — knowledge, strength and action — by which this universe was made. ॥60॥
7.1.6.61: He has no master at all, no mark, nor any ruler; he is the cause of causes and the overlord of their lords. ॥61॥
7.1.6.62: He has no begetter, nor birth from anywhere; likewise there are no causes of birth for him, those called mala, māyā and the rest. ॥62॥
7.1.6.63: He, the one, hidden in all beings and pervading everywhere, the inner Self of all beings, is called the overseer of dharma. ॥63॥
7.1.6.64: He is the dwelling of all beings, the witness, the conscious one, beyond the guṇas; the one controller of the many who are inactive and helpless by nature. ॥64॥
7.1.6.65: He is the eternal among eternals and the conscious among the conscious; the one among many, himself desireless, the Lord grants their desires. ॥65॥
7.1.6.66: Knowing the god — the cause attainable through Sāṅkhya and Yoga, the lord of the worlds — the bound soul is freed from all fetters. ॥66॥
7.1.6.67: Maker of the universe, knower of the universe, his own source, the knower, maker of time, possessor of the guṇas, the primal one, lord of the field-knowers, master of the guṇas, releaser from fetters. ॥67॥
7.1.6.68: The god who in the beginning created Brahmā and himself taught him the Vedas — having known him through the clarity of my own intellect, ॥68॥
7.1.6.69: desiring liberation from this saṃsāra, I take refuge in Śiva — partless, actionless, tranquil, faultless, stainless, ॥69॥
7.1.6.70: the supreme bridge to immortality, like a fire whose fuel has been burnt away. ॥70॥
7.1.6.71: When men shall roll up the sky like a piece of leather, then, without knowing Śiva, there will be an end of sorrow. ॥71॥
7.1.6.72: Through the power of austerity and by the grace of the god, O great sages, this knowledge befitting the highest stage of life, pure and destroying sin, ॥72॥
7.1.6.73: the supreme secret in the Vedānta, proclaimed in a former kalpa, was obtained by me from the mouth of Brahmā through the weight of good fortune. ॥73॥
7.1.6.74: This unsurpassed knowledge must not be given to one who is not tranquil, nor to a son of ill conduct, nor by any means to one who is not a disciple. ॥74॥
7.1.6.75: To the great-souled one who has supreme devotion to the god, and as to the god so to the guru — to him these teachings, when told, shine forth. ॥75॥
7.1.6.76: Therefore hear this in brief: Śiva is beyond Prakṛti and Puruṣa; at the time of creation he makes everything, and at the time of dissolution he takes it back again. ॥76॥
7.1.6.iti: Thus ends the sixth adhyāya, named The description of the knowledge of the principle of Śiva, in the Pūrva-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥6॥
7.1.7.1: The sages said: From Time everything arises, and from Time alone it perishes. Nothing at all exists anywhere that is independent of Time. ॥1॥
7.1.7.2: Time is that within whose mouth the universe, the eternal circle of saṃsāra, revolves like a wheel through the two modes of creation and dissolution. ॥2॥
7.1.7.3: Brahmā, Hari and Rudra, and likewise the other gods and asuras, having come under the order fixed by it, are not able to transgress it. ॥3॥
7.1.7.4: Dividing itself into past, present, future and so on, and wearing down creatures, it moves about freely as the supreme master, exceedingly terrifying. ॥4॥
7.1.7.5: Who is this lord Time? Under whose control is he? And who is there that would not be under his control? Tell us this, O wise one. ॥5॥
7.1.7.6: Vāyu said: The supreme radiance of Maheśvara, whose form is fashioned from the divisions such as kalā, kāṣṭhā and nimeṣa, is called the Self of Time (kālātman). ॥6॥
7.1.7.7: It is that which cannot be transgressed by any being, moving or unmoving: the Lord's power in the form of command, which governs the universe. ॥7॥
7.1.7.8: A power consisting of a fraction of a fraction of him, issuing forth from him, has passed into the great Self of Time, as heat released from fire passes into iron. ॥8॥
7.1.7.9: Therefore the universe is under the control of Time; Time is not under the control of the universe. But Time is under the control of Śiva; Śiva is not under the control of Time. ॥9॥
7.1.7.10: Since the unobstructed radiance of Śarva is established in Time, the boundary set by Time is therefore great and hard to cross. ॥10॥
7.1.7.11: Who is able to transcend Time through superior wisdom? No one oversteps what has been done by Time. ॥11॥
7.1.7.12: Even those who, having conquered by valour, rule the whole earth under a single umbrella, do not overstep Time, just as the oceans do not overstep the shore. ॥12॥
7.1.7.13: Those who, restraining the host of the senses, conquer the entire world, even they do not conquer Time; Time conquers even them. ॥13॥
7.1.7.14: Physicians versed in Āyurveda who have practised rejuvenating elixirs do not escape death, for Time is hard to overcome. ॥14॥
7.1.7.15: Relying on fortune, beauty, character, strength and lineage, a creature plans one thing; Time forcibly does another. ॥15॥
7.1.7.16: Through unforeseen encounters with the unpleasant and the pleasant, the Lord Time unites beings and separates them. ॥16॥
7.1.7.17: At the very moment that one person is miserable, another is happy. Ah, the strangeness of Time, whose nature is hard to fathom! ॥17॥
7.1.7.18: He who is young becomes old; he who is strong becomes weak; he who is prosperous becomes destitute. Wondrous is the course of Time, O brahmins. ॥18॥
7.1.7.19: Neither noble birth, nor character, nor strength, nor skill suffices for accomplishing a task if Time stands in the way. ॥19॥
7.1.7.20: Those who have protectors and are givers, attended by song and music, and those who are without protectors and eat others' food — toward all of them Time acts alike. ॥20॥
7.1.7.21: Elixirs do not bear fruit out of season, nor do medicines, even when properly administered; but those very same, gathered at the right time, quickly attain success and bestow well-being. ॥21॥
7.1.7.22: Not out of its time does one die or is born; not out of time does one attain the highest prosperity; not out of time is one happy or unhappy; there exists nothing whatever that is independent of time. ॥22॥
7.1.7.23: By Time the cool wind blows; by Time rain comes to the clouds; by Time heat subsides; by Time everything attains fruition. ॥23॥
7.1.7.24: Time is the cause of all becoming. By Time crops spring up continually; by Time crops go to destruction; by Time the world of living beings lives. ॥24॥
7.1.7.25: He who thus truly knows the nature of the Self of Time, transcending the Self of Time, beholds That which is beyond Time. ॥25॥
7.1.7.26: For whom there is neither Time, nor bondage and liberation; who is neither the Person (puruṣa), nor Nature (prakṛti), nor the universe — to that Śiva of wondrous form, the Supreme, the Supreme Lord, be salutation. ॥26॥
7.1.7.iti: Thus ends the seventh adhyāya, named The description of the greatness of Time, in the Pūrva-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥7॥
7.1.8.1: The sages said: By what measure is the count of lifespan reckoned in this world of time? And what, further, is the ultimate limit of time, which has the form of number? ॥1॥
7.1.8.2: Vāyu said: Here they declare the first measure of lifespan to be the one called nimeṣa; the limit of time, which has the form of number, is the Śāntyatītā kalā. ॥2॥
7.1.8.3: The closing movement of the eyelash is reckoned as a nimeṣa; of such nimeṣas, ten and five, that is fifteen, make a kāṣṭhā. ॥3॥
7.1.8.4: Thirty kāṣṭhās are called a kalā; thirty kalās make a muhūrta; and thirty muhūrtas they call a day-and-night. ॥4॥
7.1.8.5: With day-and-nights numbering thirty, there is a month, consisting of two fortnights. ॥5॥
7.1.8.6: A month, made up of the dark and bright fortnights, should be known as a day-and-night of the ancestors (pitṛs). ॥6॥
7.1.8.7: With six of those months there is an ayana (half-year), and two ayanas are held to be a year. That year which, by worldly measure, is known as the human year— ॥7॥
7.1.8.8: this is a divine day-and-night: such is the settled view of scripture. The southern course of the sun is the night, and the northern course the day. ॥8॥
7.1.8.9: A divine month is reckoned of thirty such day-and-nights, as with humans; likewise the year of the gods consists of twelve months. ॥9॥
7.1.8.10: Three hundred human years joined with sixty years should be known as one divine year, as declared in terms of human measure. ॥10॥
7.1.8.11: The count of the yugas proceeds by divine measure alone. The sages know of four yugas in the land of Bhārata. ॥11॥
7.1.8.12: First is the one called Kṛtayuga; after it Tretā is ordained; then Dvāpara and Kali — these are the yugas in full. ॥12॥
7.1.8.13: Four thousand years is that Kṛta yuga; its twilight (sandhyā) is of as many hundreds, and its twilight-portion (sandhyāṃśa) likewise. ॥13॥
7.1.8.14: In the other three, with their twilights and twilight-portions, the thousands and the hundreds proceed with a decrease of one each. ॥14॥
7.1.8.15: This total of twelve thousand, with the surplus, is a caturyuga; a thousand caturyugas is what is called a kalpa. ॥15॥
7.1.8.16: A manvantara is said to consist of seventy-one caturyugas; in one kalpa there are fourteen successions of Manus. ॥16॥
7.1.8.17: In this sequence, kalpas and manvantaras, together with their creatures, have passed away by hundreds and by thousands. ॥17॥
7.1.8.18: Because they are all unknowable, and moreover innumerable, a detailed account of them cannot be given in sequence. ॥18॥
7.1.8.19: A kalpa is declared to be the day of Brahmā, who was born from the Unmanifest; and a thousand kalpas is here called a year of Brahmā. ॥19॥
7.1.8.20: Eight thousand such years is a yuga of Brahmā; a thousand such yugas is a savana of the lotus-born Brahmā. ॥20॥
7.1.8.21: A thousand savanas, tripled and made threefold — so is reckoned the entire time of life of Brahmā, the Supreme One (Parameṣṭhin). ॥21॥
7.1.8.22: In his day fourteen Indras pass away; in a month, four hundred together with twenty. ॥22॥
7.1.8.23: In a year, five thousand joined with forty; and in his whole lifespan, five lakhs and forty thousand. ॥23॥
7.1.8.24: One Brahmā passes in a day of Viṣṇu, and Viṣṇu likewise in a day of Rudra; Rudra in a day of Īśvara, and likewise Īśvara in a day of the one called Sadāśiva. ॥24॥
7.1.8.25: Likewise, in the day of Śiva himself, that Sadāśiva too passes, according to the same count: five lakhs and forty thousand in the lifespan. ॥25॥
7.1.8.26: In that span this Time-Self proceeds, directed by Śiva himself — the interval of time which has here been described as the period of creation, O twice-born ones. ॥26॥
7.1.8.27: This interval of time should be known as the day of the Supreme Lord; and the night of the Supreme Lord should be known as being of entirely the same length. ॥27॥
7.1.8.28: His day is creation, and his night is known as dissolution. Yet one should understand that for him there is neither day nor night. ॥28॥
7.1.8.29: This figurative usage is employed out of desire for the welfare of the worlds. Creatures, the lords of creatures, embodied forms, gods and asuras, ॥29॥
7.1.8.30: the senses and the objects of the senses, the five great elements, the subtle elements (tanmātras), then the bhūtādi ego-principle, and intellect together with the presiding deities — ॥30॥
7.1.8.31: all these endure through the day of the wise Supreme Lord; at the end of the day they dissolve, and at the end of the night the universe comes forth again. ॥31॥
7.1.8.iti: Thus ends the eighth adhyāya, named The description of the lifespans of the three gods, in the account of the power of Time, in the Pūrva-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥8॥
7.1.9.1: The sages said: How does the Supreme Lord, having created this entire world and having withdrawn it again, perform his supreme play by his mere command? ॥1॥
7.1.9.2: What is that which came into being first? By what is this whole universe pervaded? And by what broad-bellied one is all this swallowed up again? ॥2॥
7.1.9.3: Vāyu said: From Śiva, the Lord who possesses Śakti, Śakti came forth first, higher than the state beyond peace (śāntyatīta); then Māyā, then the Unmanifest. ॥3॥
7.1.9.4: From Śakti arose the śāntyatīta state, then in order the śānti state; then the vidyā state, and from that arose the pratiṣṭhā state. ॥4॥
7.1.9.5: From the pratiṣṭhā state, in order, the nivṛtti state was produced. Thus creation, impelled by the Lord, has been described in brief. ॥5॥
7.1.9.6: Creation proceeds in direct order, and likewise the dissolution of these in reverse order. Beyond this creation designated by the five states, the Supreme Creator is acknowledged. ॥6॥
7.1.9.7: Therefore this whole universe is pervaded by the five kalās. That Unmanifest which is the cause, presided over by the Self, ॥7॥
7.1.9.8: creates everything from Mahat down to the gross elements (viśeṣa) — this too is accepted. But even there agency belongs neither to the Unmanifest nor to the Self. ॥8॥
7.1.9.9: because Prakṛti is insentient and the Puruṣa lacks knowledge. Whatever is insentient — Pradhāna, atoms and the like — ॥9॥
7.1.9.10: is that seen to act as its own agent without an intelligent cause? And the world depends on an agent, since it is an effect possessing parts. ॥10॥
7.1.9.11: Therefore he who is capable, independent, all-powerful and all-knowing, without beginning or end, endowed with great lordship — ॥11॥
7.1.9.12: he alone, Mahādeva Maheśvara, is the maker of the world, the protector and destroyer of all; he is separate from it and unattached to it. ॥12॥
7.1.9.13: The transformation of Pradhāna and the activity of the Puruṣa — everything proceeds solely by the command of him whose vow is truth. ॥13॥
7.1.9.14: This is the eternal conviction abiding in the minds of the good; but one of little understanding does not live by adopting this position. ॥14॥
7.1.9.15: From the first commencement up to the great dissolution — that whole span amounts to a hundred years of Brahmā. ॥15॥
7.1.9.16: Para is the name of the lifespan of Brahmā, who is born of the Unmanifest; that is called Para, and half of it is called Parārdha. ॥16॥
7.1.9.17: At the end of the period of two Parārdhas, when dissolution arrives, the Unmanifest takes back its own effects and abides in itself. ॥17॥
7.1.9.18: When the Unmanifest is established in itself and its modifications are withdrawn, Pradhāna and Puruṣa both abide in a state of sameness. ॥18॥
7.1.9.19: These two, the qualities tamas and sattva, remain in equilibrium, neither predominant nor deficient, interwoven with each other. ॥19॥
7.1.9.20: Then, when the qualities were in balance, undivided, with darkness prevailing, the wind stilled and all one water, nothing whatever could be discerned. ॥20॥
7.1.9.21: When this world was undiscernible, Maheśvara alone, having passed the entire supreme night of Maheśvara, then — ॥21॥
7.1.9.22: when the night had dawned, Maheśvara entered both Pradhāna and Puruṣa and agitated them through the power of Māyā. ॥22॥
7.1.9.23: Then again, by the command of the Supreme One, creation arose from the Unmanifest, the origin and dissolution of all beings. ॥23॥
7.1.9.24: Salutation to him, distinct from all the worlds, whose wondrous will surpasses the universe ever more and more, in a single fragment of whose one power the whole universe is contained, and whom the knowers of the paths (adhvan) call the Self, the lord of the paths. ॥24॥
7.1.9.iti: Thus ends the ninth adhyāya, named Being the maker of creation, preservation and dissolution, in the Pūrva-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥9॥
7.1.10.1: Vāyu said: In the beginning, from the Unmanifest presided over by Puruṣa, by the Lord's command, the evolutes beginning with intellect (buddhi) and ending with the specific elements (viśeṣa) came into being in sequence. ॥1॥
7.1.10.2: Then from those evolutes were born the three gods, Rudra, Viṣṇu and the Grandsire Brahmā, as the causes of all. ॥2॥
7.1.10.3: On them Maheśvara bestows the power of pervading the worlds on every side, unobstructed anywhere; incomparable knowledge; and everlasting lordly powers such as aṇimā (becoming minute), ॥3॥
7.1.10.4: and causal agency in the three acts called creation, maintenance and dissolution, together with sovereignty — these Maheśvara graciously grants them. ॥4॥
7.1.10.5: Again, in another kalpa, he assigned to each of them — whose minds were prone to delusion, so that they would be free of rivalry — the function of creation, protection and dissolution. ॥5॥
7.1.10.6: These, born from one another, sustain one another; they flourish through one another and are devoted to one another. ॥6॥
7.1.10.7: In some places Brahmā is praised, in some Viṣṇu, in some Rudra; by this neither their superiority nor their lordship is increased over the others. ॥7॥
7.1.10.8: Fools, obsessed with anger, revile them with words; they surely become yātudhānas and piśācas — there is no doubt. ॥8॥
7.1.10.9: The god Maheśvara transcends the three guṇas; he has a fourfold manifestation; he is with parts (sakala), the support of all, and the cause of the arising of Śakti. ॥9॥
7.1.10.10: He is the Self of this triad, of Prakṛti and of Puruṣa; having created the world in play, he abides in lordship. ॥10॥
7.1.10.11: He who is beyond everything, eternal, partless, the Supreme Lord — he alone is their support, their Self, and their presiding ruler. ॥11॥
7.1.10.12: Therefore Maheśvara, Prakṛti and likewise Puruṣa, Sadāśiva, Bhava, Viṣṇu, Brahmā — everything has Śiva as its essence. ॥12॥
7.1.10.13: From Pradhāna was first born the intellect — called khyāti, mati, mahat. From the agitation of the mahat principle, ahaṅkāra (I-making) arose in three forms. ॥13॥
7.1.10.14: Ahaṅkāra gave rise to the elements, the subtle elements and the senses. From the vaikārika ahaṅkāra, in which sattva predominates, arose the sāttvika creation. ॥14॥
7.1.10.15: That vaikārika creation proceeds all at once: the five sense organs of knowledge and the five organs of action, ॥15॥
7.1.10.16: and the eleventh there is mind, which by its own nature partakes of both. From the ahaṅkāra joined with tamas arise the elements and subtle elements. ॥16॥
7.1.10.17: Because it is the origin of the elements it is called bhūtādi. From bhūtādi comes the subtle element sound, and from that arises space (ākāśa). ॥17॥
7.1.10.18: From space arose touch; from touch the arising of air; from air, form; from that, fire; from fire, the arising of taste. ॥18॥
7.1.10.19: From taste the waters arose; from them the arising of smell; and from smell the earth was born. From the elements came everything else, moving and unmoving. ॥19॥
7.1.10.20: Because they are presided over by Puruṣa and through the favour of the Unmanifest, those evolutes from mahat to the specific elements produce the Egg. ॥20॥
7.1.10.21: When the effect and the instrument for Brahmā were fully accomplished there, then in that Egg the knower of the field (kṣetrajña), called Brahmā, came to full growth. ॥21॥
7.1.10.22: He indeed is the first embodied being; he is called Puruṣa. He, the first maker of beings, Brahmā, existed in the beginning. ॥22॥
7.1.10.23: That Lord, who identifies himself with the sacrifice, possesses an incomparable Brāhmī intellect, marked by knowledge and dispassion, which brings about dharma and sovereignty. ॥23॥
7.1.10.24: Whatever he desires in his mind is born for him from the Unmanifest, because he has brought the three guṇas under control and because they are by nature dependent on him. ॥24॥
7.1.10.25: Dividing himself threefold, he operates in the three worlds; by himself, through the three forms, he creates, devours and watches over. ॥25॥
7.1.10.26: In his Brahmā-aspect he is four-faced; in his Time-aspect he is known as the Ender; in his Puruṣa-aspect he is the thousand-headed Puruṣa — these are the three states of the Self-born. ॥26॥
7.1.10.27: In the Brahmā-state, sattva and rajas; in the Time-state, tamas and rajas; in the Viṣṇu-state, sattva alone — thus the predominance of the guṇas in the Lord is threefold. ॥27॥
7.1.10.28: In the Brahmā-state he creates the worlds; in the Time-state he withdraws them; in the Puruṣa-state he is wholly indifferent — thus the Lord's activity is threefold. ॥28॥
7.1.10.29: Thus, being divided threefold, Brahmā is called triguṇa, possessing three guṇas; being divided fourfold, he is proclaimed cāturvyūha, of four manifestations. ॥29॥
7.1.10.30: Because he is first, he is the First God; because he is unborn, he is known as Aja; since he protects all creatures, he is known as Prajāpati. ॥30॥
7.1.10.31: The golden Meru is the amnion of that great-souled one; the oceans are the fluid of the womb, and the mountains the outer membrane. ॥31॥
7.1.10.32: Within that Egg are these worlds, this whole universe, the moon and sun with the stars and planets, together with the wind. ॥32॥
7.1.10.33: The Egg is enveloped on the outside by waters tenfold its size; the waters are enveloped outside by fire tenfold theirs. ॥33॥
7.1.10.34: Fire is enveloped outside by air tenfold; air is enveloped by space, and space by bhūtādi. ॥34॥
7.1.10.35: Bhūtādi is likewise enveloped by mahat, and mahat by the Unmanifest. By these seven coverings the Egg is enveloped on the outside. ॥35॥
7.1.10.36: Enveloping this and one another, the eight Prakṛtis stand, O best of the twice-born, performing the acts of creation, preservation and destruction. ॥36॥
7.1.10.37: Thus, born from one another, the evolutes sustain one another, abiding in their sources in the relation of support and supported. ॥37॥
7.1.10.38: Just as a tortoise first stretches out its limbs and then draws them back, so the Unmanifest, having emitted the evolutes, withdraws them again. ॥38॥
7.1.10.39: Everything arising from the Unmanifest is born in forward order; but when the time of dissolution arrives, it dissolves in reverse order. ॥39॥
7.1.10.40: By the power of time alone the guṇas become unequal or equal. When the guṇas are in equilibrium, it is to be understood as dissolution; when unequal, it is called creation. ॥40॥
7.1.10.41: This, then, is the womb of Brahmā: this dense, great egg. It is declared to be Brahmā's field, and Brahmā is called the knower of the field. ॥41॥
7.1.10.42: Thus, of such eggs there should be understood to be crores upon crores by the thousands; because Pradhāna is all-pervading, they are situated across, above and below. ॥42॥
7.1.10.43: In each of them there are four-faced Brahmās, Haris and Bhavas, created likewise by Pradhāna once it has obtained the proximity of Śambhu. ॥43॥
7.1.10.44: Maheśvara is beyond the Unmanifest; the egg arises from the Unmanifest; from the egg the mighty Brahmā was born, and by him these worlds were made. ॥44॥
7.1.10.45: I have described this first creation of Pradhāna, which proceeds without prior deliberation, and also the absolute dissolution at the time of the end; both are merely the sport performed by the Lord. ॥45॥
7.1.10.46: That which is remembered as the immeasurable cause — Brahman, Pradhāna, the source from which prakṛti issues — without beginning, middle or end, of infinite power, white and deep red, joined with the Puruṣa — ॥46॥
7.1.10.47: — being productive owing to the preponderance of rajas, it creates at the beginning of time the eight evolutes, the causes of the growth and continuity of the world, and likewise devours them at the time of the end. ॥47॥
7.1.10.48: Whatever maintenance and whatever renewed activity there is of the causes established in prakṛti — all that comes about by the mere resolve of Maheśvara, whose glory is not of prakṛti. ॥48॥
7.1.10.iti: Thus ends the tenth adhyāya, named The state of the cosmic egg, in the Pūrva-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥10॥
7.1.11.1: The sages said: Tell us about all the Manvantaras and the different kinds of kalpa in full, and, within them, the intermediate creation and the re-creation. ॥1॥
7.1.11.2: Vāyu said: For Brahmā, who unfolds through the reckoning of time, a parārdha is declared as his span; and he has another period of the same length. At its end the world is withdrawn again. ॥2॥
7.1.11.3: In each and every day of that first-born Brahmā, O illustrious ones, there are fourteen successions of the Manus. ॥3॥
7.1.11.4: Because they are beginningless, endless and not knowable in their entirety, the Manvantaras and kalpas cannot be described one by one in words. ॥4॥
7.1.11.5: And even if all of them were told, what benefit would there be here for you who listen to my words? Therefore I do not undertake to describe them separately. ॥5॥
7.1.11.6: Among the kalpas, in the very kalpa that is now current, the creations and re-creations take place; these I shall tell in brief. ॥6॥
7.1.11.7: The kalpa that is now current is called by name Vārāha. In this one too, O best of the twice-born, there are fourteen Manus. ॥7॥
7.1.11.8: Seven beginning with Svāyambhuva, and seven beginning with Sāvarṇika; among them the seventh Manu, named Vaivasvata, is now reigning. ॥8॥
7.1.11.9: In all the Manvantaras the processes of creation and destruction are largely alike: so the knowing person should infer. ॥9॥
7.1.11.10: When the previous kalpa had come to its close, when the wind of Time had set in, and the trees and forests had been torn up by their roots, ॥10॥
7.1.11.11: when the god Fire was burning the three worlds like straw, when the earth had been drenched by rain and the oceans had overflowed their shores, ॥11॥
7.1.11.12: when all the directions were submerged in the vast flood of water, and with its waters' restless tossing, with circling arms of waves, ॥12॥
7.1.11.13: then, when the waters of dissolution had begun their fierce dance, Brahmā, having become Nārāyaṇa, slept peacefully on the water. ॥13॥
7.1.11.14: And the sages recited this mantra, a verse concerning Nārāyaṇa. Hear it, O best of sages, and its meaning based on the syllables. ॥14॥
7.1.11.15: The waters are called nārāḥ, for the waters are the offspring of Nara. Since they are his abode (ayana), he is therefore known as Nārāyaṇa. ॥15॥
7.1.11.16: The Siddhas dwelling in Janaloka, with joined palms, approached the lord of the gods, who was in a sleep consisting of Śiva-yoga, ॥16॥
7.1.11.17: and these divine beings awakened him with hymns at the time of dawn, just as formerly, at the beginning of creation, the Vedas awakened the Lord. ॥17॥
7.1.11.18: Then, awakened, he rose from his bed lying in the midst of the waters and looked out over all the directions, his eyes heavy with yogic sleep. ॥18॥
7.1.11.19: He then saw nothing that was distinct from his own self; sitting as if in astonishment, he fell into deep thought. ॥19॥
7.1.11.20: Where is that blessed one, the lovely and vast Earth, with her many kinds of great mountains, rivers, cities and forests? ॥20॥
7.1.11.21: Thinking thus, Brahmā could not discover where the Earth was. Then he called to mind his father, the blessed three-eyed one. ॥21॥
7.1.11.22: Through remembering Bhava, the god of gods of immeasurable splendour, the lord of the Earth came to know that the Earth was submerged in the water. ॥22॥
7.1.11.23: Then Prajāpati, wishing to lift up the Earth, called to mind the divine boar form, suited to sporting in water. ॥23॥
7.1.11.24: A form with a body like a great mountain, roaring like a great rain-cloud, resembling a dark-blue cloud, with a blazing sound, terrifying; ॥24॥
7.1.11.25: with stout, rounded, dense shoulders, broad and raised hips, short rounded thighs and shanks, and very sharp circular hooves; ॥25॥
7.1.11.26: shining like a ruby, with round fearsome eyes, a rounded, long, huge body, and resplendent with stiff, erect ears; ॥26॥
7.1.11.27: whirling the ocean of dissolution with its forceful in-breaths and out-breaths, and handsome with cheeks and shoulders covered by a glistening thick mane; ॥27॥
7.1.11.28: adorned with jewels, colourful ornaments and great gems, lofty and shining like a mass of clouds with lightning. ॥28॥
7.1.11.29: Assuming that vast, immeasurable boar form, the Creator entered the netherworld (Rasātala) in order to lift up the Earth. ॥29॥
7.1.11.30: Then that mountain-like boar shone exceedingly, just as the boar who went to the foot of Maheśa in the form of the liṅga. ॥30॥
7.1.11.31: Then that upholder of the Earth lifted up the Earth submerged in the water, holding her close with his two tusks, and emerged from Rasātala. ॥31॥
7.1.11.32: Seeing him, the sages and Siddhas dwelling in Janaloka rejoiced, danced, and showered flowers upon his head. ॥32॥
7.1.11.33: The body of the Great Boar, covered with flowers, shone like a lofty collyrium mountain with fireflies falling upon it. ॥33॥
7.1.11.34: Then the Boar, the all-pervading lord, having brought the great Earth to her proper position, resumed his own form and established her firmly. ॥34॥
7.1.11.35: Having levelled the Earth and placing the mountains on it, he fashioned the four worlds beginning with Bhū as before. ॥35॥
7.1.11.36: Thus, having raised the great Earth together with its mountains from the depths in the midst of the great ocean of dissolution and set it above, the maker of all (Viśvakarmā) created again the world, moving and unmoving. ॥36॥
7.1.11.iti: Thus ends the eleventh adhyāya, named Creation and the rest, in the Pūrva-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥11॥
7.1.12.1: Vāyu said: While he was then contemplating creation deliberately (with prior thought), at the time of deep meditation, a delusion consisting of darkness appeared. ॥1॥
7.1.12.2: Tamas, Moha, Mahāmoha, Tāmisra and the one called Andha -tāmisra — this fivefold Ignorance (avidyā) arose from the great-souled one. ॥2॥
7.1.12.3: As the self-conscious one meditated, creation was established fivefold, covered on all sides exceedingly by darkness, like a seed in a pot. ॥3॥
7.1.12.4: It was unilluminated outside and within, inert and without consciousness. Therefore their intellect, mouths and organs are covered. ॥4॥
7.1.12.5: Therefore those of enclosed nature, the immovables (trees and mountains), are called the primary (mukhya). Brahmā, seeing this first creation of such a kind to be ineffective, ॥5॥
7.1.12.6: became displeased in mind and thought of a second. As he meditated on creation, the horizontal-current (tiryak-srotas) creation came forth. ॥6॥
7.1.12.7: Then were born the animals, illumined within but covered outside, of beastly nature; and they follow the wrong path. ॥7॥
7.1.12.8: Knowing that too to be ineffective, he thought of another creation. Then arose the sāttvika creation of the gods, of upward current. ॥8॥
7.1.12.9: They abound in happiness and joy, are not covered outside or within, are luminous outside and within, and conscious by their very nature. ॥9॥
7.1.12.10: Then, as he meditated, from the unmanifest arose the downward-current creation, effective for the purpose, named human, abounding in sorrow. ॥10॥
