7.1.12.11: They are luminous outside and within, with an excess of tamas and predominance of rajas. The fifth, the Anugraha creation, is arranged fourfold: ॥11॥
7.1.12.12: by misconception, by capacity, by contentment, and likewise by perfection. They all are non-possessive and again delight in sharing. ॥12॥
7.1.12.13: And the devourers and those without good conduct, beginning with the bhūtas, are declared. The first creation of Brahmā Parameṣṭhin is that of Mahat. ॥13॥
7.1.12.14: The second is of the tanmātras; that is called the creation of elements (bhūta-sarga). The third, the vaikārika, is known as the creation of the senses. ॥14॥
7.1.12.15: Thus this creation of Prakṛti came about without prior intellect. The fourth is the primary creation; the immovables are known as the primary ones. ॥15॥
7.1.12.16: That which was called the horizontal current, of animal birth, is the fifth. Then the sixth, of upward current, is known as the creation of gods. ॥16॥
7.1.12.17: Then the creation of those of downward current is the seventh; that is the human. The eighth is the Anugraha creation; the Kaumāra is known as the ninth. ॥17॥
7.1.12.18: The first three creations are prākṛta; they are not preceded by intellect. The five beginning with the primary are vaikṛta and proceed with intellect. ॥18॥
7.1.12.19: First Brahmā created mind-born sons equal to himself: Sananda, Sanaka, and the learned Sanātana, ॥19॥
7.1.12.20: and Ṛbhu and Sanatkumāra — these the Prajāpati created first. All of them are to be known as yogins, free from passion and free from envy. ॥20॥
7.1.12.21: With minds attached to the Lord, they did not set their minds on creation. When Sanaka and the others, indifferent to creation, had departed, ॥21॥
7.1.12.22: Brahmā, wishing to create again, performed supreme austerity. But while he was thus practising austerity, nothing came about. ॥22॥
7.1.12.23: Then after a long time anger arose from distress. From the eyes of him, overcome by anger, teardrops fell. ॥23॥
7.1.12.24: Then from those teardrops bhūtas and pretas came into being. Seeing all of them born from tears, Brahmā reproached himself. ॥24॥
7.1.12.25: An intense swoon arose in him, born of anger and indignation. Swooning, overcome by anger, the Prajāpati gave up his life-breaths. ॥25॥
7.1.12.26: Then Rudra, lord of the life-breaths, the blessed Nīlalohita, appeared from the mouth of the lord to bestow incomparable grace. ॥26॥
7.1.12.27: The lord Īśvara made himself tenfold and onefold. Those great souls, made tenfold and onefold, were addressed by him: ॥27॥
7.1.12.28: You have been created by me, children, for the sake of favouring the worlds. Therefore, for the establishment and welfare of the whole world ॥28॥
7.1.12.29: and for the propagation of progeny, strive untiringly. Thus addressed, they wept and ran about in all directions. ॥29॥
7.1.12.30: From weeping (rodana) and running (drāvaṇa) they are known by name as the Rudras. Those who are Rudras are indeed the life-breaths; those who are the life-breaths are great-souled. ॥30॥
7.1.12.31: Then the compassionate Maheśvara, son of Brahmā, gave back the life-breaths to the dead god Brahmā Parameṣṭhin. ॥31॥
7.1.12.32: Rudra, lord of the universe, his face joyful at the return of the lord's life-breaths, spoke supreme words to Brahmā: ॥32॥
7.1.12.33: Do not fear, do not fear, O greatly fortunate Viriñci, teacher of the worlds. Your life-breaths have been revived by me; rise happily, O you of good vows. ॥33॥
7.1.12.34: Hearing that charming speech as if experienced in a dream, and slowly gazing at Hara with eyes radiant like blooming lotuses, ॥34॥
7.1.12.35: Brahmā, his breaths thus restored, with joined palms spoke words addressed to him in an affectionate, deep voice: ॥35॥
7.1.12.36: By your mere sight you delight my mind. Who are you, standing in cosmic form, elevenfold? ॥36॥
7.1.12.37: Hearing his words, Maheśvara, lord of the gods, replied, touching Brahmā with his two very soothing hands: ॥37॥
7.1.12.38: Know me as the Supreme Self, who has come to be your son. And these eleven Rudras have come to protect you well. ॥38॥
7.1.12.39: Therefore, shaking off this intense swoon through my grace, awaken; you should create beings as before. ॥39॥
7.1.12.40: Thus addressed by the Lord, Brahmā became glad at heart; the universal self praised the Supreme Lord with a hymn of eight names. ॥40॥
7.1.12.41: Brahmā said: Salutation to you, O Lord Rudra, whose immeasurable radiance is that of the sun. Salutation to Bhava, the god who is taste (rasa), whose self consists of water. Salutation to Śarva, whose form is the earth, ever fragrant. ॥41॥
7.1.12.42: Salutation to you, Īśa, the Vasu, whose self consists of touch; and to the Lord of creatures (Paśupati), the fire of surpassing brilliance; salutation to you, Bhīma, whose form is the sky, whose essence is sound alone. ॥42॥
7.1.12.43: Salutation to Ugra, of fierce form, whose self is the sacrificer. Salutation be to Mahāśiva, Soma, whose embodiment is nectar. ॥43॥
7.1.12.44: Having thus praised Mahādeva, Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds, entreated the Lord of the universe with words preceded by obeisance. ॥44॥
7.1.12.45: O Lord, ruler of what has been and what is to be, my son, Maheśvara, destroyer of Ananga (Kāma): you were born from my body for the purpose of creation. ॥45॥
7.1.12.46: Therefore, O Lord of the world, give help in every way to me, who am engaged in this great task; you ought to create excellent offspring. ॥46॥
7.1.12.47: Thus entreated by him, the god Rudra, crusher of Tripura, Śaṅkara, accepted those words, saying simply, so be it. ॥47॥
7.1.12.48: Then the blessed Brahmā, having greeted him, who was pleased, and being permitted by him to create, likewise created other beings. ॥48॥
7.1.12.49: He created by mind alone Marīci, Bhṛgu, Aṅgiras, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Dakṣa, Atri and Vasiṣṭha; and before them Brahmā created Dharma and Saṅkalpa. ॥49॥
7.1.12.50: These are proclaimed as the twelve first sons of Brahmā, born together with Rudra, the ancient householders. ॥50॥
7.1.12.51: Their twelve lineages are divine, accompanied by hosts of gods, rich in offspring, active in rites, and adorned with great sages. ॥51॥
7.1.12.52: Then the Creator (Vidhi), together with Rudra, desiring to create the fourfold group — gods, asuras, ancestors (pitṛs) and humans — these called the waters... ॥52॥
7.1.12.53: Brahmā, concentrating for the purpose of creation, yoked his self in yoga. From his mouth he produced the gods, and from his sides the ancestors. ॥53॥
7.1.12.54: From his hips he produced all the asuras, and from his generative organ the humans; from his excretory part were born the rākṣasas, possessed by hunger. ॥54॥
7.1.12.55: Those sons, mostly of tamas and rajas, were mighty night-wanderers; serpents, yakṣas, bhūtas and gandharvas were likewise born. ॥55॥
7.1.12.56: Birds were created from his sides; winged creatures he created from his chest; from his mouth he made goats, and from his flank he fashioned the serpents. ॥56॥
7.1.12.57: And from his feet he created horses along with elephants, śarabhas, gavayas, deer, camels, mules, nyaṅku antelopes and other species. ॥57॥
7.1.12.58: Herbs, fruits and roots were born from his body-hairs. The Gāyatrī metre, the Ṛc, the Trivṛt stoma, the Rathantara sāman, ॥58॥
7.1.12.59: and the Agniṣṭoma among sacrifices he fashioned from his first (eastern) mouth. The Yajus formulas, the Triṣṭubh metre, the fifteenfold stoma, ॥59॥
7.1.12.60: the Bṛhat sāman and the Uktha he created from his southern mouth. The Sāmans, the Jagatī metre, the seventeenfold stoma, ॥60॥
7.1.12.61: the Vairūpya and the Atirātra he created from his western mouth. The twenty-onefold stoma, the Atharvan, and the Āptoryāma, ॥61॥
7.1.12.62: the Anuṣṭubh and the Vairāja he created from his northern mouth. Beings high and low were born from his limbs: ॥62॥
7.1.12.63: yakṣas, piśācas, gandharvas, and likewise the hosts of apsarases; humans, kinnaras, rākṣasas, birds, cattle, wild animals and serpents, ॥63॥
7.1.12.64: and this whole imperishable world, moving and unmoving. Whatever actions they had taken up in the former creation, ॥64॥
7.1.12.65: those very actions they take up again when created again and again: violent or non-violent, gentle or cruel, righteous or unrighteous, true or false. ॥65॥
7.1.12.66: Imbued with that former disposition they take it up; therefore that is what pleases each. The diversity among the great elements, among the objects of the senses, and among forms of release, ॥66॥
7.1.12.67: and the assignment of beings to their functions — the Ordainer himself established. The names and forms of beings and the elaboration of the natural creations ॥67॥
7.1.12.68: that Grandfather fashioned in the beginning from the words of the Veda alone. The names of the seers, and whatever modes of life are in the Vedas, ॥68॥
7.1.12.69: those very names and functions the Unborn gave to those born at the end of the night of dissolution. Just as in each season the marks of that season, of various forms, appear in succession, ॥69॥
7.1.12.70: those same ones are seen again, so too are the conditions at the beginnings of the yugas. Such is the creation of the worlds by the Self-born, arising from the instruments of creation, ॥70॥
7.1.12.71: the transformation of Prakṛti herself, beginning with Mahat and ending with the particulars (viśeṣas); graced with the light of moon and sun, adorned with planets and stars, ॥71॥
7.1.12.72: It is adorned with rivers, oceans and mountains, and likewise with various other delightful, prosperous lands. ॥72॥
7.1.12.73: In that forest of Brahman the unmanifest, all-knowing Brahmā moves. This tree springs from the unmanifest seed and stands upon the grace of Īśvara; ॥73॥
7.1.12.74: intellect (buddhi) is its trunk and great branches, the inner senses its hollows; the great elements are its measure, the particulars its spotless leaves; ॥74॥
7.1.12.75: rich in the fine blossoms of dharma and adharma, yielding the fruits of pleasure and pain, the sustenance of all beings — this is the eternal Brahma-tree. ॥75॥
7.1.12.76: The sages declare heaven to be his head, the sky his navel, moon and sun his eyes, the directions his ears, and the earth his feet; he is of inconceivable self, the leader of all beings. ॥76॥
7.1.12.77: From his mouth the brāhmaṇas were born; from the front part of his chest the kṣatriyas; the vaiśyas from his thighs, and the śūdras from his feet: all the varṇas were born from his body. ॥77॥
7.1.12.iti: Thus ends the twelfth adhyāya, named Creation, in the Pūrva-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥12॥
7.1.13.1: The sages said: You have told of the birth of Bhava, the Supreme Self, from the mouth of the four-faced one Brahmā; about this a doubt arises in us. ॥1॥
7.1.13.2: He is the best of gods, the odd-eyed, the radiant, the trident-bearer Hara, whose self is Time, the blessed Rudra, wearer of matted locks, the blue-red one — ॥2॥
7.1.13.3: who, enraged, when the end of the age has arrived, destroys this world together with Brahmā, together with Viṣṇu, and even Fire; ॥3॥
7.1.13.4: to whom Brahmā and Viṣṇu make obeisance out of fear; this contractor of the worlds, under whose control those two remain; ॥4॥
7.1.13.5: this god who of old created Brahmā and Viṣṇu from his own body — he indeed is the lord who ever secures their acquisition and preservation. ॥5॥
7.1.13.6: How did that blessed Rudra, the primordial, ancient god, Śambhu, become the son of Brahmā, whose birth is from the Unmanifest? ॥6॥
7.1.13.7: We have also heard before that these two of Rudra, Prajāpati and Viṣṇu, were created mutually, each from the other's body. ॥7॥
7.1.13.8: How, again, is there a manifestation from one another of these two who are the causes of all beings, in the relation of subordinate and principal? ॥8॥
7.1.13.9: There is nothing you have not asked, nor anything you have in any way not heard; being the disciple of the Lord, you remember everything. ॥9॥
7.1.13.10: Tell the truth of it, just as the mighty Brahmā told it to the sages. We, dear sir, are full of faith and eager to hear the true glory of the Lord. ॥10॥
7.1.13.11: Vāyu said: Fittingly has this been asked, O brahmins, by you who are skilled in questioning. When I asked this very thing long ago, the Grandfather told it to me. ॥11॥
7.1.13.12: That I shall now relate: how Rudra arose, and how, again, Brahmā and Viṣṇu originated from each other. ॥12॥
7.1.13.13: Those three, whose nature is causal, were born directly from Maheśvara; they are the causes of the creation, maintenance and end of the universe, moving and unmoving. ॥13॥
7.1.13.14: Endowed with supreme lordship, brought into being by the Supreme Lord, ever presided over by his power, they are capable of carrying out his work. ॥14॥
7.1.13.15: All three were first appointed by the Father to three tasks: Brahmā to creation, Hari to protection, and Rudra likewise to destruction. ॥15॥
7.1.13.16: Even so, out of rivalry with one another, desiring to surpass one another, having pleased their own father, the Supreme Lord, with austerity, ॥16॥
7.1.13.17: and having obtained power in full through the grace of that Supreme One, Rudra first, in another aeon, created Brahmā and Nārāyaṇa. ॥17॥
7.1.13.18: In another aeon, again, Brahmā, who pervades the world, created Rudra and Viṣṇu; and the blessed Viṣṇu in turn created Rudra and Brahmā. ॥18॥
7.1.13.19: Again Brahmā created Nārāyaṇa, and again Bhava created Brahmā. Thus, aeon after aeon, Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Maheśvara — ॥19॥
7.1.13.20: are born from one another, wishing one another's welfare. With reference to the events of each of those aeons, by the great sages ॥20॥
7.1.13.21: their greatness is told, arising from their mutual origination. Hear the wondrous, holy tale of them, which frees from sin, ॥21॥
7.1.13.22: which took place in the Tatpuruṣa aeon of Brahmā, the Supreme One. Long ago, in the aeon called Meghavāhana, Nārāyaṇa by name ॥22॥
7.1.13.23: became a cloud and bore the earth for a thousand divine years. Observing that devotion of Viṣṇu, the preceptor of the whole world, ॥23॥
7.1.13.24: Sarva, with his whole being, bestowed imperishable power on him. Having then obtained power from Śiva, the lord of all, Viṣṇu, the self of all, ॥24॥
7.1.13.25: the blessed Viṣṇu created the universe along with the creator of the universe Brahmā. Seeing that splendour of Viṣṇu, the Grandfather, who had been created by him, ॥25॥
7.1.13.26: seized by intense jealousy, laughing, said this: Go, Viṣṇu. I know the cause of your creation. There is One greater than us both — that is Rudra; of this there is no doubt. ॥26॥
7.1.13.27: By the grace of that God above gods, the Supreme One, you, the lord, are the first creator and, in truth, the protector. ॥27॥
7.1.13.28: I too, having propitiated with austerity Rudra, the leader of the gods, shall create the whole world together with you; of this there is no doubt. ॥28॥
7.1.13.29: Having thus reproached Viṣṇu, the blessed lotus-born one, having reached Śaṅkara through austerity, made this petition: ॥29॥
7.1.13.30: O Blessed One, lord of the god of gods, lord of the universe, Maheśvara, Viṣṇu is born from your left side, and I indeed arose from your right side. ॥30॥
7.1.13.31: Even so, Acyuta created the whole world together with me. Out of jealousy he was reproached by me, he being strong through the power of reliance on you. ॥31॥
7.1.13.32: His surpassing devotion to you, Maheśvara, is not greater than my devotion, since the origin of us both, from you alone, is alike. ॥32॥
7.1.13.33: Just as you formerly showed grace to him for his devotion, so, Śaṅkara, you should grant all that to me as well. ॥33॥
7.1.13.34: Thus petitioned by him, the blessed destroyer of Bhaga's eyes, that treasury of compassion, justly gave everything to him as well. ॥34॥
7.1.13.35: Having thus obtained from the Lord himself, in an instant, the state of being the self of all, Brahmā then hastened, approached, and saw Puruṣottama, ॥35॥
7.1.13.36: in his abode in the Ocean of Milk, in a bright, sun-like, divine aerial palace set with gold and jewels, fashioned by his mind, ॥36॥
7.1.13.37: lying on the couch of Ananta's coils, lotus-eyed, four-armed, of noble form, adorned with every ornament, ॥37॥
7.1.13.38: bearing conch and discus, gentle, with a face like the moon's disc, the god with the Śrīvatsa on his chest, smiling graciously and sweetly, ॥38॥
7.1.13.39: his lotus feet reddened by the touch of Dharā's (the Earth's) soft lotus hands, lying in yogic sleep like the nectar of the Ocean of Milk, ॥39॥
7.1.13.40: him who, through tamas, is called Kālarudra; through rajas, the one born of the golden egg, Brahmā; through sattva, the all-pervading Viṣṇu; and in the state beyond qualities, Maheśvara. ॥40॥
7.1.13.41: Having seen that Person, Brahmā boldly said this: I shall swallow you, O Viṣṇu, just as you swallowed me before. ॥41॥
7.1.13.42: Hearing those words of his, the mighty-armed one, having awakened, looked up at the Grandfather and smiled slightly. ॥42॥
7.1.13.43: At that moment Viṣṇu was swallowed by that great-souled one, and at once was effortlessly brought forth by Brahmā from between his brows. ॥43॥
7.1.13.44: At that moment the Lord himself, adorned with the moon, though formless, assumed a form in order to see the power of those two as well. ॥44॥
7.1.13.45: He who had formerly granted them a boon came, to bestow incomparable grace, to the place where these two, Brahmā and Nārāyaṇa, stood. ॥45॥
7.1.13.46: Then the two, delighted and yet afraid, praised the god out of wonder, and bowed to him many times from afar with great reverence. ॥46॥
7.1.13.47: Bhava too, the Lord, bearer of the Pināka bow, having shown favour to these two, vanished even as they were reverently watching. ॥47॥
7.1.13.iti: Thus ends the thirteenth adhyāya, named The account of the creation of Brahmā and Viṣṇu, in the Pūrva-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥13॥
7.1.14.1: Vāyu said: I shall explain, for each kalpa, the cause of Rudra's manifestation, by which Brahmā's creation proceeds with an unbroken line of descent. ॥1॥
7.1.14.2: In kalpa after kalpa, Brahmā, born from the cosmic egg, having created beings, became bewildered and deeply distressed because the beings did not increase. ॥2॥
7.1.14.3: To allay his distress and for the increase of beings, in each of those kalpas Rudra, whose self is Time, lord of the Rudra-hosts, ॥3॥
7.1.14.4: directed by the Supreme Lord, Maheśa, the blue-and-red one, becoming a son of Brahmā — yet Brahmā's younger brother — bestows grace upon Brahmā. ॥4॥
7.1.14.5: He indeed is the blessed Lord, a mass of radiance, free from affliction, without beginning or end, the sustainer, the withdrawer of beings, the all-pervading one. ॥5॥
7.1.14.6: Endowed with supreme sovereignty, infused with the nature of the Supreme Lord, ever presided over by his power, and marked with his very emblems; ॥6॥
7.1.14.7: bearing his names, having his form, capable of performing his works, conducting himself like him, and carrying out his commands; ॥7॥
7.1.14.8: radiant like a thousand suns, adorned with a digit of the moon, with serpents for necklace, armlets and bracelets, and a girdle of muñja grass; ॥8॥
7.1.14.9: resplendent with fragments of the skulls of Jalandhara, Viriñca (Brahmā) and Indra; his tawny face and hair wet with the lofty waves of the Gaṅgā; ॥9॥
7.1.14.10: lovely with the broken tusk-tip of the Earth-upholder Boar pressed at his side; his earring coiled into a ring at the edge of his left ear; ॥10॥
7.1.14.11: riding forth on a great bull, with a voice like a great rain-cloud, blazing like a great fire, of great strength and valour. ॥11॥
7.1.14.12: Thus Maheśvara, of terrible and mighty form, the son of Brahmā, gives knowledge to Brahmā and carries out creation together with him. ॥12॥
7.1.14.13: Therefore, by Rudra's grace, in every kalpa the Prajāpati's creation of beings proceeds perpetually in the form of a continuous stream. ॥13॥
7.1.14.14: Once, when requested by Brahmā to create, the all-pervading Nīlalohita created by his mind beings all like himself: ॥14॥
7.1.14.15: with matted locks, fearless, blue-necked, three-eyed, free from old age and death, bearing blazing tridents as their chief weapons. ॥15॥
7.1.14.16: By them the whole fourteen-fold world was covered. Seeing those manifold Rudras, the Grandsire said to Rudra: ॥16॥
7.1.14.17: Salutation to you, Lord of the gods of gods. Do not create such beings. Create other beings, subject to death — may it go well with you. ॥17॥
7.1.14.18: Thus addressed, the Supreme Lord, laughing, said to Brahmā: I have no such creation; you create the inauspicious beings. ॥18॥
7.1.14.19: But these great-souled, mighty ones whom I created by the mind will all move about together with me, for they are all worthy of sacrifice. ॥19॥
7.1.14.20: Having said this to the world-maker (Brahmā), Hara, lord of all beings, stood with the Rudras, his mind withdrawn from the creation of beings. ॥20॥
7.1.14.21: From then on that god does not beget auspicious beings; he remains as Sthāṇu, of upward-drawn seed, until the dissolution of beings. ॥21॥
7.1.14.iti: Thus ends the fourteenth adhyāya, named The appearance of Rudra, in the Pūrva-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥14॥
7.1.15.1: Vāyu said: When the creatures created by the Creator (Vedhas) did not multiply again, Brahmā then resolved to bring about creation born of sexual union. ॥1॥
7.1.15.2: Since the race of women had not previously come forth from the Lord, the Grandsire was unable to bring about creation by sexual union. ॥2॥
7.1.15.3: Then he formed a resolve leading to a firm decision on the matter: For the very increase of the creatures, the Supreme Lord must be asked. ॥3॥
7.1.15.4: Without his grace these creatures will not multiply. Having reflected thus, the Soul of the universe began to perform austerity. ॥4॥
7.1.15.5: Then he meditated on the primal supreme Śakti, endless, the bringer-forth of the worlds, primordial, most subtle, pure, reachable through devotion, enchanting, ॥5॥
7.1.15.6: beyond qualities, beyond the manifold world, partless, untroubled, ever delighting in the Lord, eternal, always at the side of the Lord. ॥6॥
7.1.15.7: Meditating in his heart on the blessed Tryambaka together with that supreme Śakti, Brahmā performed supreme austerity. ॥7॥
7.1.15.8: By the intense austerity of that Parameṣṭhin, steadfast in yoga, the Father was well pleased in a very short time indeed. ॥8॥
7.1.15.9: Then, entering a certain form by a portion of himself, the god Hara himself, having become Ardhanārīśvara (the Lord who is half woman), went to him. ॥9॥
7.1.15.10: Seeing that supreme god, beyond darkness, imperishable, without a second, indescribable, invisible to those whose selves are unperfected, ॥10॥
7.1.15.11: the ordainer of all worlds, lord of the lords of all worlds, united with the supreme Śakti who ordains all worlds, ॥11॥
7.1.15.12: beyond reasoning, without semblance, immeasurable, ageless, firm, unmoving, without qualities, tranquil, the abode of infinite greatness, ॥12॥
7.1.15.13: all-pervading, giver of all, free from every manifestation of being and non-being, freed from all comparison, the refuge, eternal Śiva — ॥13॥
7.1.15.14: Brahmā prostrated like a staff, rose, and with joined palms, with hymns full of faith and humility, pleasing to hear, endowed with refinement, ॥14॥
7.1.15.15: hymns whose every sense was joined to truth, amplified by the meaning of the Vedas, and conveying subtle meanings, he praised the god and the goddess. ॥15॥
7.1.15.16: Brahmā said: Victory to you, O God, O Mahādeva! Victory, O Lord, O Maheśvara! Victory, O best in all virtues! Victory, O sovereign of all the gods! ॥16॥
7.1.15.17: Victory, O you who are auspicious by nature! Victory, O leader of Prakṛti! Victory to you who are far beyond Prakṛti! Victory, O you naturally beautiful one! ॥17॥
7.1.15.18: Victory, O you of unfailing great Māyā! Victory, O you whose wishes never fail! Victory, O you of unfailing great sport! Victory, O you of unfailing great strength! ॥18॥
7.1.15.19: Victory, O Mother of the whole world! Victory, O you who consist of the whole world! Victory, O sustainer of the whole world! Victory, O friend of the whole world! ॥19॥
7.1.15.20: Victory, O you of eternal sovereignty! Victory, O you of eternal abode! Victory, O you of eternal form! Victory, O you of eternal followers! ॥20॥
7.1.15.21: Victory, O creator of the three selves! Victory, O protectress of the three selves! Victory, O destroyer of the three selves! Victory, O mistress of the three selves! ॥21॥
7.1.15.22: Victory, O you on whose glance the expansion of the causes of the world depends! Victory, O you by the fire arising from whose glance of indifference the material world is consumed! ॥22॥
7.1.15.23: Victory, O you unknowable even to the gods and others, radiant to the subtle vision of the self! Victory, O sovereign through the Śakti of the gross self! Victory, O you who pervade the moving and unmoving! ॥23॥
7.1.15.24: Victory, O you in whom the aggregate of the world's principles is arranged as many and as one! Victory, O you whose host of excellent followers stand upon the heads of the asuras! ॥24॥
7.1.15.25: Victory, O you most skilled in arranging the protection of those who take refuge in you! Victory, O you who uproot the sprouting of the poison-tree of saṃsāra! ॥25॥
7.1.15.26: Victory, O you whose lordship, valour and heroism are displayed only partially in particular places! Victory, O you who stand outside the universe and have cast down the glory of others! ॥26॥
7.1.15.27: Victory, O supreme nectar of the practice of the five categories (pañcārtha) that you propounded! Victory, O you whose nature is a stream of the nectar of the knowledge of the five categories! ॥27॥
7.1.15.28: Victory, O best physician for the great disease of most terrible saṃsāra! Victory, O moonlight dispelling the veil of darkness of beginningless impurity and ignorance! ॥28॥
7.1.15.29: Victory, O fire of time for Tripura! Victory, O Tripurabhairavī! Victory, O you free from the three guṇas! Victory, O crusher of the three guṇas! ॥29॥
7.1.15.30: Victory, O first omniscient one! Victory, O awakener of all! Victory, O you of abundant divine limbs! Victory, O granter of what is prayed for! ॥30॥
7.1.15.31: Where, O God, is your supreme abode, and where our trifling speech? Even so, O Blessed One, forgive me as I babble out of devotion. ॥31॥
7.1.15.32: Having made his supplication with such hymns, the four-faced creator of all (Viśvakarman) bowed again and again to Rudra and Rudrāṇī. ॥32॥
7.1.15.33: This excellent, meritorious hymn uttered by Brahmā, named Ardhanārīśvara, increases the joy of Śiva and Śivā. ॥33॥
7.1.15.34: Whoever recites this with devotion, with a desire for anything whatever, obtains that fruit because of the pleasure of Śiva and Śivā. ॥34॥
7.1.15.35: I ever bow down to the two Śaṅkaras, who bring into being all the worlds and beings, whose bodies are free from birth and destruction, and who bear the forms of the best of men and a young woman. ॥35॥
7.1.15.iti: Thus ends the fifteenth adhyāya, named The praise of Śiva and Śivā, in the Pūrva-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥15॥
7.1.16.1: Vāyu said: Then the god Mahādeva spoke, with a voice that had the sound of a great rain-cloud and whose syllables were sweet, deep, auspicious and smooth, ॥1॥
7.1.16.2: whose words were rich in meaning, which bore the marks of royalty, and which was able to bring about the beginning, protection and dissolution of all things, ॥2॥
7.1.16.3: and which was preceded by a most charming, noble and sweet smile — with such a voice the Lord, greatly pleased, addressed the Maker of the universe, Brahmā. ॥3॥
7.1.16.4: Īśvara said: Child, child, most fortunate one, my son, Grandfather, the full weight of your words is indeed known to me. ॥4॥
7.1.16.5: You have now performed austerity solely for the increase of creatures. I am pleased with this austerity, and I grant what you desire. ॥5॥
7.1.16.6: Having spoken these supremely gracious and naturally sweet words, Hara, the best of gods, created the Goddess from a part of his own body — ॥6॥
7.1.16.7: the Goddess endowed with divine qualities, whom the knowers of Brahman call the supreme Śakti of Bhava, the Highest, the Supreme Self; ॥7॥
7.1.16.8: in whom birth, death, old age and the like truly do not exist; she, Bhavānī, manifested, it is said, from the body of Bhava. ॥8॥
7.1.16.9: She from whom words turn back together with the mind and the senses appeared as though born from a part of her husband's body. ॥9॥
7.1.16.10: She who abides pervading this entire world by her greatness — that Goddess was wondrously seen as though embodied. ॥10॥
7.1.16.11: She deludes this whole world by her māyā; she herself was born from Īśvara, though in ultimate truth she is unborn. ॥11॥
7.1.16.12: She whose supreme nature is not within the range even of the gods, the Mistress of the universe and of the immortals, was separated from her husband's body. ॥12॥
7.1.16.13: Seeing her — the Supreme Ruler, the great Mistress of all worlds, omniscient, all-pervading, subtle, beyond manifestation as being or non-being, ॥13॥
7.1.16.14: the Supreme one, illuminating this entire world with her radiance — Virāṭ Brahmā, bowing to the great Goddess, entreated her. ॥14॥
7.1.16.15: Brahmā said: O Goddess, you who consist of the whole world, I was created by the God in the beginning and appointed to the creation of beings; I create the whole world. ॥15॥
7.1.16.16: O Goddess, all the gods and others were fashioned by me through the mind; though created again and again, they do not increase. ॥16॥
7.1.16.17: From now on, making creation arise from couples, I wish to increase all my creatures. ॥17॥
7.1.16.18: Formerly the imperishable race of women had not come forth from you; therefore I have no power to create the race of women. ॥18॥
7.1.16.19: Indeed, the origin of all powers is from you; therefore I entreat you, who bestow every power on all beings everywhere — ॥19॥
7.1.16.20: you alone, the boon-giving Māyā, the Mistress of the gods, do I entreat: for the increase of the moving and the unmoving, O all-pervading one, with one portion of yourself, ॥20॥
7.1.16.21: become the daughter of Dakṣa, my son, O remover of worldly existence. Thus was the Goddess entreated by Brahmā, whose source is Brahman. ॥21॥
7.1.16.22: She emitted from between her brows a single Śakti, of radiance equal to her own. Looking at her, Hara, the best of the god of gods, said to her with a laugh: ॥22॥
7.1.16.23: Having been propitiated by Brahmā's austerity, do for him as he desires. Accepting that command of the Supreme Lord on her head, she, ॥23॥
7.1.16.24: the Goddess, at Brahmā's word, became the daughter of Dakṣa. Having thus given to Brahmā the incomparable Śakti, whose form is Brahman, ॥24॥
7.1.16.25: she entered the body of the God, and the God vanished. From that time on, enjoyment in woman was established in this world, ॥25॥
7.1.16.26: and the creation of beings, O chiefs of brahmins, proceeds through sexual union. Brahmā too, O foremost sages, attained joyful contentment. ॥26॥
7.1.16.27: All this has been told to you — the arising of the Goddess's Śakti — which increases merit and is worthy to be heard, narrated in connection with the creation of beings. ॥27॥
7.1.16.28: Whoever constantly recites this arising of the Goddess's Śakti obtains all merit and gains auspicious sons. ॥28॥
7.1.16.iti: Thus ends the sixteenth adhyāya, named The emergence of the Devī, the Śakti, in the Pūrva-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥16॥
7.1.17.1: Vāyu said: Thus, having obtained from the Lord (Īśvara) Himself the supreme, eternal Śakti, Prajāpati, wishing to bring about creation arising from sexual union, ॥1॥
7.1.17.2: himself became a woman with one half and a man with the other half. From the half that was woman, Śatarūpā was born. ॥2॥
7.1.17.3: Brahmā created Virāj; he became the man from the other half. He indeed is called the first man, Svāyambhuva Manu. ॥3॥
7.1.17.4: That goddess Śatarūpā, having performed very arduous austerity, obtained as husband Manu himself, of blazing fame. ॥4॥
7.1.17.5: From him Śatarūpā bore two sons, Priyavrata and Uttānapāda, the best of those who have sons, ॥5॥
7.1.17.6: and two highly fortunate daughters, from whom these creatures were born. One is to be known as Ākūti; the other is remembered as Prasūti. ॥6॥
7.1.17.7: The lord Svāyambhuva gave that Prasūti to Dakṣa, and he gave Ākūti to Prajāpati Ruci. ॥7॥
7.1.17.8: In Ākūti an auspicious twin pair was born to Ruci, the mind-born: Yajña and Dakṣiṇā, by whom the world was set in motion. ॥8॥
7.1.17.9: In Prasūti, the daughter of Svāyambhuva, the lord Dakṣa begot twenty-four daughters, mothers of the worlds: ॥9॥
7.1.17.10: Śraddhā, Lakṣmī, Dhṛti, Puṣṭi, Tuṣṭi, Medhā and Kriyā, Buddhi, Lajjā, Vapus, Śānti, Siddhi, and Kīrti the thirteenth. ॥10॥
7.1.17.11: The lord Dharma accepted these daughters of Dakṣa as wives. Remaining after them were eleven younger ones with beautiful eyes: ॥11॥
7.1.17.12: Khyāti, Satī, then Sambhūti, Smṛti, Prīti and Kṣamā, Sannati and Anasūyā, Ūrjā, Svāhā and Svadhā. ॥12॥
7.1.17.13: Bhṛgu, Śarva, Marīci, Aṅgiras, Pulaha, Kratu, Pulastya, Atri, Vasiṣṭha, Pāvaka (Fire) and likewise the Pitṛs — ॥13॥
7.1.17.14: these sages took the maidens beginning with Khyāti, O best of sages. The thirteen sons beginning with Kāma and ending with Yaśas — ॥14॥
7.1.17.15: were born to Dharma from those wives beginning with Śraddhā, sons culminating in great happiness. And in the lineage of Adharma, from Hiṃsā, offspring culminating in sorrow — ॥15॥
7.1.17.16: there arose Nikṛti and the others, sons bearing the marks of adharma. They have neither wives nor sons; all are regarded as without restraint. ॥16॥
7.1.17.17: This was the tāmasa creation, which arose as the restrainer of dharma. Satī, the daughter of Dakṣa and beloved of Rudra, ॥17॥
7.1.17.18: on the occasion of the reviling of her husband, abandoned her body born of Dakṣa, having reproached Dakṣa and Dakṣa's wife together with their kinsmen; ॥18॥
7.1.17.19: she was born of Menā as the daughter of the mountain Himavat. And how Rudra, having seen that Satī, created Rudras equal in splendour to himself, ॥19॥
7.1.17.20: how he created countless Rudras — that too has been told. From Khyāti, wife of Bhṛgu, was born Lakṣmī, beloved of Nārāyaṇa, ॥20॥
7.1.17.21: and the two gods Dhātṛ and Vidhātṛ, upholders of the Manvantaras. Their sons, grandsons and further descendants, by hundreds and thousands, ॥21॥
7.1.17.22: who passed away in the Svāyambhuva Manvantara — all of them are considered Bhārgavas. Sambhūti, wife of Marīci, bore Paurṇamāsa, ॥22॥
7.1.17.23: and four daughters. Their descendants were very great; in their line was born Kaśyapa, the father of many sons. ॥23॥
7.1.17.24: Smṛti, the wife of Aṅgiras, bore two sons, Āgnīdhra and Śarabha, and also four daughters. ॥24॥
7.1.17.25: Their sons and grandsons who have passed away were in thousands. In Prīti, the wife of Pulastya, a son Dantāgni was born, who in a former birth in the Svāyambhuva Manvantara is remembered as Agastya. ॥25॥
7.1.17.26: His many descendants are renowned as the Paulastyas. Kṣamā bore sons to Prajāpati Pulaha: ॥26॥
7.1.17.27: Kardama, Āsuri and Sahiṣṇu — these three, all with the splendour of the three sacred fires, whose lineage is well established. ॥27॥
7.1.17.28: Sannati, the wife of Kratu, bore sons equal to Kratu. They had neither wives nor sons; all of them were celibate (ūrdhvaretas). ॥28॥
7.1.17.29: Those sixty thousand are remembered as the Vālakhilyas; surrounding the Sun, they go before Anūru (Aruṇa). ॥29॥
7.1.17.30: Anasūyā, the wife of Atri, bore five Ātreyas and a daughter named Śruti, the mother of Śaṅkhapada. ॥30॥
7.1.17.31: Satyanetra, Havya, Āpomūrti, Śanaiścara, and Soma the fifth — these are proclaimed as the five Ātreyas. ॥31॥
7.1.17.32: The sons and grandsons of those great-souled Ātreyas passed away in the Svāyambhuva Manvantara by hundreds and thousands. ॥32॥
7.1.17.33: In Ūrjā seven sons were born to Vasiṣṭha, and their elder sister was Puṇḍarīkā of slender waist. ॥33॥
7.1.17.34: Rajas, Gātra, Ūrdhvabāhu, Savana, and he who is Anaya, Sutapas and Śukra — these seven are remembered as the seven Ṛṣis. ॥34॥
7.1.17.35: The clans, by their names, of those great-souled Vāsiṣṭhas that passed away in the Svāyambhuva Manvantara numbered hundreds of arbudas (hundreds of millions). ॥35॥
7.1.17.36: Thus this creation of the Ṛṣis together with its continuation has been declared in brief; it cannot be told in detail, O twice-born ones. ॥36॥
7.1.17.37: That Fire (Vahni), of the nature of Rudra, the mind-born son of Brahmā — his beloved Svāhā obtained three sons of immeasurable vigour: ॥37॥
7.1.17.38: Pāvaka, Pavamāna and Śuci — these are the three. Pavamāna is the fire produced by friction; Pāvaka is remembered as the lightning fire; ॥38॥
7.1.17.39: and that which blazes in the sun is called Śuci, the solar fire. Havyavāha, Kavyavāha and Saharakṣas — these three ॥39॥
7.1.17.40: are respectively the sons of those three, the fires of the gods, the Pitṛs and the Asuras. The sons and grandsons of these are forty-nine in all. ॥40॥
7.1.17.41: Established in the three kinds of rites, the optional, the occasional and the perpetual, all these fires should be known as ascetics, and likewise all as bearers of vows. ॥41॥
7.1.17.42: All of them have Rudra as their very self, and all are devoted wholly to Rudra. Therefore whatever is offered by anyone into the mouth of the fire, ॥42॥
7.1.17.43: all that is given with Rudra as its intended recipient; there is no doubt about this. Thus has the settled account of the fires been recounted exactly as it is. ॥43॥
7.1.17.44: O brahmins, after this I shall speak of the Pitṛs (ancestors), not at great length. Since the six seasons are the abode of those Pitṛs who preside over those abodes, ॥44॥
7.1.17.45: therefore the seasons are the Pitṛs: such is the Vedic scripture. Since in the seasons all beings, stationary and moving, are born, ॥45॥
7.1.17.46: therefore these Pitṛs are called Ārtavas (seasonal ones); so it is heard. Thus, of these Pitṛs who preside over the seasons and times, ॥46॥
7.1.17.47: the great-souled ones, possessing their own sovereign power, abide here in association with the clouds. The Pitṛs are remembered as of two kinds: the Agniṣvāttas and the Barhiṣads. ॥47॥
7.1.17.48: Respectively, they are householders who did not perform sacrifice and who did perform sacrifice. And Svadhā bore to the Pitṛs two daughters renowned in the world: ॥48॥
7.1.17.49: Menā and Dharaṇī, by whom this universe is upheld. Menā is the daughter of the Agniṣvāttas, Dharaṇī the daughter of the Barhiṣads. ॥49॥
7.1.17.50: Menā, the wife of Himavat, bore Maināka and Krauñca, and Gaurī and Gaṅgā, who purify through the embrace of Bhava's body. ॥50॥
7.1.17.51: Dharaṇī, the wife of Meru, bore a son, Mandara, endowed with divine herbs and with wondrous, beautiful ridges. ॥51॥
7.1.17.52: That very glorious Mandara, son of Meru, through the power of his austerity became the very dwelling of Śiva, the Lord Śrīkaṇṭha. ॥52॥
7.1.17.53: That Dharaṇī further bore three renowned daughters: Velā, Niyati, and the third, Āyati. ॥53॥
7.1.17.54: Āyati and Niyati were the two wives of the two sons of Bhṛgu; their lineage was told to you earlier, in the account of the Svāyambhuva Manvantara. ॥54॥
7.1.17.55: Velā bore from the Ocean one blameless daughter named Savarṇā, the Ocean's daughter (Sāmudrī), who became the wife of Prācīnabarhis. ॥55॥
7.1.17.56: Sāmudrī bore ten sons to Prācīnabarhis, all named the Pracetases, masters of the science of archery. ॥56॥
7.1.17.57: Dakṣa, who had been in the Svāyambhuva Manvantara of old, became their son in the Manvantara of Cākṣuṣa Manu, through the curse of Tryambaka. ॥57॥
7.1.17.58: Thus, O brahmins, the lineages of these great-souled sons of Brahmā, Dharma and the others, neither too briefly nor too extensively, in due order, ॥58॥
7.1.17.59: these divine lineages have been described by me, accompanied by hosts of gods, active in rites, rich in progeny, and adorned with great prosperity. ॥59॥
7.1.17.60: This arrangement of creatures, arising from the Prajāpatis, cannot be enumerated even in hundreds of crores of years. ॥60॥
7.1.17.61: And the lineage of kings, too, proceeds in two branches: the Solar dynasty and the Lunar dynasty, most holy on earth. ॥61॥
7.1.17.62: Ikṣvāku, Ambarīṣa, Yayāti, the descendants of Nahuṣa and others, those of holy fame who are heard of here, are also born in those dynasties. ॥62॥
7.1.17.63: And there are other royal sages endowed with various powers. What fruit is there in recounting those ancient ones, already told before and not here enumerated? ॥63॥
7.1.17.64: Moreover, considering that glorifying others here and there in the course of a narrative about the Lord is not approved by the virtuous, I am not inclined to say much. ॥64॥
7.1.17.65: Creation and the rest have been told only incidentally and to illuminate the Lord's power; hence there is no need here for their full elaboration. ॥65॥
7.1.17.iti: Thus ends the seventeenth adhyāya, named The account of creation, in the Pūrva-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥17॥
7.1.18.1: The sages said: How did the Goddess, the daughter of Dakṣa, having given up her body born of Dakṣa, become long ago the daughter of Himavat in the womb of Menā? ॥1॥
7.1.18.2: And how was Rudra reviled by the great-souled Dakṣa? What, too, was the occasion there by which Bhava came to be reviled? ॥2॥
7.1.18.3: And how was Dakṣa born, through the curse of Bhava, formerly in the period of Manu Cākṣuṣa? Tell us, O Māruta. ॥3॥
7.1.18.4: Vāyu said: Listen, I shall relate the conduct of the small-minded Dakṣa, which, out of sinfulness and heedlessness, brought disgrace upon all the gods. ॥4॥
7.1.18.5: Long ago, once, all the gods and demons, the Siddhas and the supreme sages went to a peak of Himavat to see Īśāna. ॥5॥
7.1.18.6: Then the God and the Goddess, both seated on divine thrones, granted their sight to those gods and the rest, O best of the twice-born. ॥6॥
7.1.18.7: At that very time Dakṣa too went there with the immortals, to see his son-in-law Hara and the Goddess Satī, his own daughter. ॥7॥
7.1.18.8: Then, when Dakṣa had arrived, the God together with the Goddess, because of their own exalted dignity, never showed him any special regard above the gods and the others. ॥8॥
7.1.18.9: In him, who did not know her supreme nature and was deluded into thinking of her merely as his daughter, enmity toward her arose. ॥9॥
7.1.18.10: Then, driven by that very enmity and by fate, Dakṣa, when consecrated for a sacrifice, did not invite Bhava, hating her as well. ॥10॥
7.1.18.11: Having invited all his other sons-in-law in due order, he paid them ample honours by the hundreds, to each separately. ॥11॥
7.1.18.12: Then, hearing from Nārada's mouth that they had thus assembled, Rudrāṇī informed Rudra and went to her father's house. ॥12॥
7.1.18.13: Then a divine aerial chariot was brought near, facing all directions, rich in auspicious marks, easy to mount, immense and captivating, ॥13॥
7.1.18.14: shining like refined gold, adorned with varied gems, with an excellent canopy made of pearls, and decorated with garlands and festoons, ॥14॥
7.1.18.15: with turrets of refined gold, surrounded by hundreds of jewelled pillars, with steps fashioned of diamond, and archways with coral columns, ॥15॥
7.1.18.16: spread with flowered cloths, with a great seat of varied gems, its windows set with diamond lattices, and a floor of gems without a gap, ॥16॥
7.1.18.17: its front adorned with a banner white as a cloud, bearing the emblem of a great bull and charming with its jewelled staff, ॥17॥
7.1.18.18: its great door guarded by invincible lords of the Gaṇas, their bodies protected by jewelled armour, each holding a variegated staff in one hand, ॥18॥
7.1.18.19: and surrounded by many women skilled in drum, cymbal, song and the like, flute and lute, elegant in dress and ornaments. ॥19॥
7.1.18.20: The Great Goddess mounted it together with her dear companions. Two chowrie-fans for her, charming with diamond handles, ॥20॥
7.1.18.21: two lovely maidens of Rudra took up and both fanned her. Then, between the two chowries, the Goddess's face shone ॥21॥
7.1.18.22: like a lotus between two swans fighting each other. Over her crest Sumālinī, ॥22॥
7.1.18.23: full of love, held a moon-like parasol fringed with strung pearls. That radiant parasol shone above the Goddess's face ॥23॥
7.1.18.24: like the orb of the moon above a vessel of nectar. Then Śubhāvatī, seated in front, with a smiling face, ॥24॥
7.1.18.25: entertained Satī with the pastime of a game of dice. Suyaśā, holding the Goddess's lovely sandals adorned with gems ॥25॥
7.1.18.26: placed between her breasts, then served the Goddess. Another, with lovely golden limbs, took up a shining mirror; ॥26॥
7.1.18.27: another a palm-leaf fan, and yet another a betel box; some lovely lady held a charming pet parrot in her hand; ॥27॥
7.1.18.28: one carried very lovely and fragrant flowers; one lotus-eyed lady carried a jewel casket; ॥28॥
7.1.18.29: and one, again, carried unguent, fine blossoms and auspicious collyrium; and others, each like them, performing their respective fitting duties, ॥29॥
7.1.18.30: surrounding that Great Goddess, served her on all sides. Amid them the Supreme Goddess shone exceedingly, ॥30॥
7.1.18.31: like the autumn crescent moon amid an assembly of stars. Then, right after the sound rising from the conch, ॥31॥
7.1.18.32: the loud kettledrum signalling departure was beaten. Then sweet instruments, along with sounds keeping the rhythm, ॥32॥
7.1.18.33: and unstruck instruments resounded, and hundreds of kāhala horns. Of the armed lords of the Gaṇas, equal in splendour to Maheśa, ॥33॥
7.1.18.34: eight hundred thousand then went in front. In their midst, mounted on a bull, like a lord (guru) riding an elephant, ॥34॥
7.1.18.35: went the glorious leader of the Gaṇas, Nandīśvara, honoured by Soma. The divine drums, deep-toned and divinely delightful, sounded in the sky. ॥35॥
7.1.18.36: All the sages danced, the Siddhas and yogins rejoiced, and the clouds poured a shower of flowers upon the canopy. ॥36॥
7.1.18.37: Then, joined everywhere along the way by hosts of gods and others, Maheśvarī entered her father's house as if in an instant. ॥37॥
7.1.18.38: Seeing her, Dakṣa grew angry and—for the sake of his own ruin—offered her a disrespectful honour, lower even than that given to her younger sisters. ॥38॥
7.1.18.39: Then the moon-faced Goddess Ambikā spoke to her father, seated in the assembly, words that were fitting, composed and dignified. ॥39॥
7.1.18.40: The Goddess said: The God under whose command all beings from Brahmā down to the Piśācas abide—that God, father, has now, it seems, not been worshipped according to rule. ॥40॥
7.1.18.41: Let that be. Why, disregarding me, your elder daughter, left unhonoured, have you performed such worship of the others? You have done a blameworthy thing. ॥41॥
7.1.18.42: Thus addressed, Dakṣa, impatient with anger, said to her: My younger daughters are superior to you, more distinguished, and worthy of honour. ॥42॥
7.1.18.43: And their husbands are gladly esteemed by me; all of them are superior in virtues even to your husband, the Three-eyed (Tryambaka). ॥43॥
7.1.18.44: Śarva is stubborn-minded and tāmasic, and you have taken refuge in him; therefore I disdain you, for Bhava is hostile to me. ॥44॥
7.1.18.45: Thus addressed, the Goddess, angered, spoke to her father Dakṣa, while all those present in the sacrificial assembly were listening. ॥45॥
7.1.18.46: Without cause, O Dakṣa, you revile with words my husband, in whom no fault whatever has arisen, who is directly the Great Lord of the worlds. ॥46॥
7.1.18.47: The thief of knowledge, the betrayer of the teacher, and the reviler of the Lord of the Vedas—these are all great sinners and deserve punishment: so says the scripture. ॥47॥
7.1.18.48: Therefore a terrible punishment, fully befitting this exceedingly grave sin of yours, will suddenly befall you by fate. ॥48॥
7.1.18.49: Since the God of gods, Tryambaka, has not been worshipped by you, know for certain that your corrupt lineage is destroyed. ॥49॥
7.1.18.50: Having spoken thus to her father, the angered Satī, casting off all fear, abandoned the body born of him and went to the mountain Himavat. ॥50॥
7.1.18.51: That glorious best of mountains, in whom the fruit of merit had come to fruition, had performed long and arduous austerity for that very purpose. ॥51॥
7.1.18.52: Therefore the Goddess favoured that lord of mountains, and of her own will, by her own yogic power (yogamāyā), made him her father. ॥52॥
7.1.18.53: When Satī departed after reproaching Dakṣa, who was overwhelmed with fear, then the mantras vanished and thereupon the sacrifice was ruined. ॥53॥
7.1.18.54: Hearing of the Goddess's departure, the Destroyer of Tripura became angry with Dakṣa and the sages, and cursed them. ॥54॥
7.1.18.55: Since, O Dakṣa, on my account the blameless Satī was disdained, while all your other daughters were honoured together with their husbands, ॥55॥
7.1.18.56: therefore in the Vaivasvata Manvantara all these sons-in-law of yours will be born together, not from a womb, in Brahmā's sacrifices. ॥56॥
7.1.18.57: You will become a human king in the line of Cākṣuṣa, the grandson of Prācīnabarhis and the son of Pracetas. ॥57॥
7.1.18.58: Even there, O evil-minded one, I will obstruct you again and again, even in rites connected with dharma, wealth and desire. ॥58॥
7.1.18.59: Thus addressed by Rudra of immeasurable splendour, Dakṣa, grief-stricken, abandoned his body born of Svayambhū and fell to the earth. ॥59॥
7.1.18.60: Then in the Cākṣuṣa Manvantara Dakṣa was born as Prācetasa, the grandson of Prācīnabarhis and the son of the Pracetases. ॥60॥
7.1.18.61: Bhṛgu and the others too were born in the period of Manu Vaivasvata, at Brahmā's sacrifice, bearing bodies derived from Varuṇa. ॥61॥
7.1.18.62: Then, during the reign of Manu Vaivasvata, Maheśa created an obstruction for the evil-souled Dakṣa when he engaged in a rite for the sake of dharma. ॥62॥
7.1.18.iti: Thus ends the eighteenth adhyāya, named Satī gives up her body, in the Pūrva-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥18॥
7.1.19.1: The sages said: How did Maheśa create an obstacle for the evil-minded Dakṣa, who had set out on a sacrifice for the sake of dharma? This we wish to know. ॥1॥
7.1.19.2: Vāyu said: When the mountain Himavat was delighted, having attained, through the power of his austerity, the status of father to the Goddess, who is the mother even of the whole world, ॥2॥
7.1.19.3: and when the God too, having married her and dwelling on the peak of Himavat, was sporting with her, after a very long time had passed, ॥3॥
7.1.19.4: when the Vaivasvata Manvantara had arrived, Dakṣa, son of the Pracetases, himself set about intending to sacrifice with the horse-sacrifice. ॥4॥
7.1.19.5: Then Dakṣa performed the sacrifice on the slope of Himavat, at Gaṅgādvāra, an auspicious place frequented by sages and Siddhas. ॥5॥
7.1.19.6: Then all the gods, headed by Śakra, assembling together, resolved to go to that sacrifice of his. ॥6॥
7.1.19.7: The Ādityas, Vasus, Rudras, Sādhyas together with the hosts of Maruts, the Ūṣmapas, the Somapas, the Ājyapas and likewise the Dhūmapas, ॥7॥
7.1.19.8: the two Aśvins, the Pitṛs, and likewise other great sages — all of them, together with Viṣṇu, arrived as sharers in the sacrifice. ॥8॥
7.1.19.9: Seeing the whole host of gods gone there without Īśvara, Dadhīca, filled with indignation, spoke thus to Dakṣa. ॥9॥
7.1.19.10: Dadhīca said: By worshipping one unworthy of worship, and by not worshipping those worthy of worship, a man incurs great sin — of this there is no doubt. ॥10॥
7.1.19.11: Where the wicked are honoured and the good likewise despised, there a terrible punishment wrought by the gods falls at once. ॥11॥
7.1.19.12: Having said this, the brahmin-sage again spoke to Dakṣa: Why do you not worship the Lord, the master of beings (Paśupati), who is worthy of worship? ॥12॥
7.1.19.13: Dakṣa said: I have many Rudras, trident in hand and with matted locks, who stand as the eleven; I know of no other Maheśvara. ॥13॥
7.1.19.14: Dadhīca said: What fruit is there from these other immortals being worshipped at the sacrifice, if Rudra, the king of this sacrifice, is not worshipped by you? ॥14॥
7.1.19.15: He who is the creator of Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Maheśa, the imperishable Lord, whose servitude all beings from Brahmā down to the Piśācas profess; ॥15॥
7.1.19.16: who is beyond the Prakṛtis and beyond the Puruṣa, who is contemplated by sages versed in yoga and seers of truth; ॥16॥
7.1.19.17: who is the imperishable, supreme Brahman, which is non-being and also being-and-non-being, without beginning, middle or end, beyond reasoning, eternal; ॥17॥
7.1.19.18: Maheśvara, who is the creator, the destroyer and the sustainer — apart from him, Śaṅkara himself, I see no other worthy of honour in the sacrifice. ॥18॥
7.1.19.19: Dakṣa said: This entire oblation in the golden vessel, purified by rite and mantra, I today offer, having apportioned it for the sacred fire, as the share of Viṣṇu, the lord of the sacrifice, the peerless master. ॥19॥
7.1.19.20: Dadhīca said: Since Rudra, the lord of the lords of all gods, has not been worshipped, therefore, O Dakṣa, this sacrifice of yours will not be completed. ॥20॥
7.1.19.21: Having spoken these words in anger, Dadhīca, best of sages, left that place and went to his own hermitage. ॥21॥
7.1.19.22: Even after that sage had left, the gods did not abandon Dakṣa, because the impending calamity had necessarily to be experienced. ॥22॥
7.1.19.23: At that very time, O brahmins, the Goddess, having learned all this from the Lord, urged the God to burn up Dakṣa's sacrifice. ॥23॥
7.1.19.24: Urged by the Goddess, the God, wishing to destroy Dakṣa's sacrifice, suddenly created the hero Vīrabhadra, lord of the Gaṇas, ॥24॥
7.1.19.25: a god with a thousand faces, a thousand lotus-eyes, bearing a thousand maces and holding a thousand arrows in his hands, ॥25॥
7.1.19.26: with trident, axe and club in hand, bearing a blazing bow, holding discus and thunderbolt, terrible, with the half-moon as his crest, ॥26॥
7.1.19.27: his hands flashing with the thunderbolt, his hair blazing like lightning, bearing a huge mouth dreadful with fangs, and a great belly, ॥27॥
7.1.19.28: with a tongue like lightning, pendulous lips, a roar like clouds and the ocean, wearing a tiger-skin streaming with much blood, ॥28॥
7.1.19.29: with circular earrings touching both cheeks, his crest adorned with rows of garlands of the heads of eminent immortals, ॥29॥
7.1.19.30: adorned with jingling anklets, armlets and great golden ornaments, shining with heaps of gems, his chest covered with a pearl necklace, ॥30॥
7.1.19.31: with valour equal to great Śarabhas, tigers and lions, with a leisurely gait like that of a splendid rutting elephant, ॥31॥
7.1.19.32: with a lustre like a conch, a yak-tail whisk, jasmine, the moon and lotus-fibre, like the king of mountains covered with snow come to life in bodily form, ॥32॥
7.1.19.33: encircled by garlands of flames, adorned with shining pearls, blazing with splendour like the fire at the end of the age. ॥33॥
7.1.19.34: That lord of the Gaṇas, going down on his knees to the ground, bowed with joined palms, and then stood at the side of the God of gods. ॥34॥
7.1.19.35: And from wrath the Goddess created the auspicious Bhadrakālī, the great sovereign goddess, to go along with him as witness of her own deed. ॥35॥
7.1.19.36: Seeing Vīrabhadra standing there, resembling the fire of dissolution, together with Bhadrā, Śaṅkara said, may it be well. ॥36॥
7.1.19.37: And he, together with the goddess, submitted to Maheśvara: Command me, O Mahādeva — what task shall I do? ॥37॥
7.1.19.38: Then the slayer of Tripura, wishing to please the daughter of Himavat, spoke to the mighty-armed Vīrabhadra in a voice of resounding tone. ॥38॥
7.1.19.39: Mahādeva said: Destroy at once the sacrifice of Dakṣa, son of the Pracetases; this task is yours, O lord of the Gaṇas, together with Bhadrakālī. ॥39॥
7.1.19.40: I too, together with her, staying near the hermitage of Raibhya, shall watch, O lord of the Gaṇas, your irresistible valour. ॥40॥
7.1.19.41: Where the trees in Kanakhala, near Gaṅgādvāra, on the golden-peaked mountain, resemble Meru and Mandara, ॥41॥
7.1.19.42: in that region Dakṣa's sacrifice is now taking place. Suddenly bring about the destruction of that sacrifice; do not delay. ॥42॥
7.1.19.43: When this had been said by the god, the goddess, daughter of the lord of the snow-mountain, gazing at Bhadra and Bhadrā as a cow gazes at her own calf, ॥43॥
7.1.19.44: and embracing them and kissing them on the head as she would Ṣaḍvadana, smiling, she herself spoke most sweet words. ॥44॥
7.1.19.45: The Goddess said: O child Bhadra, greatly fortunate one, of great strength and valour, you have been born for my pleasure; wipe away my anger. ॥45॥
7.1.19.46: Without inviting the Lord of sacrifice, he has become engaged in the sacrificial rite out of enmity; therefore, O lord of the gaṇas, shatter that Dakṣa and his sacrifice. ॥46॥
7.1.19.47: By my command, O Bhadra, turn the glory of the sacrifice into misfortune, and having killed that sacrificer, O child, wreak havoc together with Bhadrā. ॥47॥
7.1.19.48: Placing on his head that command of Śiva and Śivā, whose deeds are wondrous, as if it were a garland in its entirety, and bowing, Bhadra began to set out. ॥48॥
7.1.19.49: Then this blessed one, enraged, who has made his dwelling in the abode of ghosts, Vīrabhadra, the great god, remover of the goddess's anger, ॥49॥
7.1.19.50: created from his hair-pores lords of gaṇas called Romajas, and from the region of his right arm a hundred crore lords of gaṇas, ॥50॥
7.1.19.51: likewise from his feet, thighs, back, sides, mouth, throat, private parts, ankles, the middle of his head, neck, face and belly. ॥51॥
7.1.19.52: Then the whole world, together with the expanse of the sky, was covered by those auspicious lords of gaṇas whose valour equalled Bhadra's. ॥52॥
7.1.19.53: All of them had a thousand arms and a thousand weapons in their hands; all were followers of Rudra, all of splendour equal to Rudra. ॥53॥
7.1.19.54: Holding tridents, spears and maces in their hands, bearing chisels, stones and rocks, resembling Kālāgnirudra, three-eyed and wearing matted locks, ॥54॥
7.1.19.55: they swooped violently through the sky by hundreds, riding on lions; and those born of Bhadra roared great roars like thunderclouds. ॥55॥
7.1.19.56: Surrounded thus by those Bhadras, the blessed Bhadra shone like Kālabhairava at the end of time, accompanied by hundreds of doomsday fires. ॥56॥
7.1.19.57: In their midst, mounting the lord of bulls, the bull-bannered blessed Bhadra went forth, like Bhava riding a white cloud. ॥57॥
7.1.19.58: When Bhadra had mounted the bull, Bhasitaprabha, holding a white chowrie, bore a pearl umbrella over him. ॥58॥
7.1.19.59: Then Bhasitaprabha shone at Bhadra's side like the blessed lord of mountains at the side of the teacher of the whole world. ॥59॥
7.1.19.60: And Bhadra too shone because of him, chowrie in hand, as the bearer of the excellent trident shines with the gentle crescent moon. ॥60॥
7.1.19.61: Bhānukampa, of great splendour, adorned with gold and gems, blew a white, auspicious, lovely conch before Bhadra. ॥61॥
7.1.19.62: Divine kettledrums resounded with a dense heavenly din; clouds by the hundreds rained a shower of flowers on his head. ॥62॥
7.1.19.63: And breezes, kin to the fragrance of blossoming, honey-filled flowers, blew along the way, wafting favourably to his path. ॥63॥
7.1.19.64: Then all the lords of gaṇas, intoxicated and arrogant with martial strength, danced, rejoiced, roared, laughed, shouted and sang. ॥64॥
7.1.19.65: Then Bhadra, standing amid the Bhadra-gaṇas, shone together with Bhadrā, as Tryambaka shines amid the Rudra-gaṇas with Ambikā. ॥65॥
7.1.19.66: At that very moment the mighty-armed Vīrabhadra, with his great retinue, entered Dakṣa's golden sacrificial enclosure. ॥66॥
7.1.19.67: Then Bhadra, chief of the gaṇas, entered the performance-ground of that foremost of sacrifices arranged by Dakṣa, like Rudra at the end of time wishing to burn up the world. ॥67॥
7.1.19.iti: Thus ends the nineteenth adhyāya, named The birth of Vīrabhadra, in the Pūrva-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥19॥
7.1.20.1: Vāyu said: Then he saw the great sacrificial session of the gods of boundless might, headed by Viṣṇu, adorned with colourful banners. ॥1॥
7.1.20.2: It was well strewn with fine darbha grass, its fires well kindled, and adorned with shining golden sacrificial vessels. ॥2॥
7.1.20.3: Its many rites were being well performed according to the procedure seen in the Veda by sages skilled in sacrifice, who carried out the acts properly. ॥3॥
7.1.20.4: It was rich with thousands of divine women, attended by troops of Apsarases, filled with the sounds of flutes and vīṇās, and swelled by the chanting of the Vedas. ॥4॥
7.1.20.5: Having seen Dakṣa's sacrifice, the valiant and mighty Vīrabhadra then roared a lion's roar, deep like a thundercloud. ॥5॥
7.1.20.6: Then a great kilakilā shout was raised at the sacrifice by the lords of the Gaṇas, as if filling the sky, surpassing the roar of the ocean. ॥6॥
7.1.20.7: Seized by that great sound, all the heaven-dwellers fled in all directions in fear, their garments and ornaments slipping off. ॥7॥
7.1.20.8: Has great Meru broken? Is the earth splitting apart? What is this, what is this? — so the gods babbled excitedly. ॥8॥
7.1.20.9: As great elephants in a dense forest die on hearing the roar of lions, so some, hearing such a sound, gave up their lives from fear. ॥9॥
7.1.20.10: The mountains crumbled, the earth shook, the winds whirled about, and the ocean was agitated. ॥10॥
7.1.20.11: The fires did not blaze, nor did the sun shine; the planets, the lunar mansions and the stars gave no light. ॥11॥
7.1.20.12: At that very moment the lord Bhadra (Vīrabhadra) reached that splendid sacrificial enclosure together with the Bhadras (his attendants) and with Bhadrā (Bhadrakālī). ॥12॥
7.1.20.13: Seeing him, Dakṣa, though utterly terrified, stood as if firm and spoke words as if in anger: Who are you? What do you want here? ॥13॥
7.1.20.14: Hearing those words of the wicked Dakṣa, Vīrabhadra of great splendour, whose voice was deep as a thundercloud, ॥14॥
7.1.20.15: looking at Dakṣa, the gods and the priests as though smiling, spoke fitting words, full of meaning and unperturbed. ॥15॥
7.1.20.16: Vīrabhadra said: We are all followers of Śarva of boundless splendour; we have come desiring our share. Let our share be given to us. ॥16॥
7.1.20.17: But if no share has been allotted to us in the sacrifice, let the reason for it be stated — or else let the immortals fight with me. ॥17॥
7.1.20.18: Thus addressed by the lord of the Gaṇas, the gods led by Dakṣa said: The Mantras are our authority; we are not the masters here. ॥18॥
7.1.20.19: The Mantras said: O gods, your minds are struck by delusion, since you do not worship Maheśvara, who deserves the first share. ॥19॥
7.1.20.20: Though told so by the Mantras, all those gods, utterly bewildered in mind, did not give the share to Bhadra, wishing to keep him excluded. ॥20॥
7.1.20.21: When their own statement, true and beneficial, proved futile, the Mantras then went from there to the eternal world of Brahmā. ॥21॥
7.1.20.22: Then the chief of the Gaṇas said to the gods led by Viṣṇu: You, proud of your strength, have not taken the Mantras as authority. ॥22॥
7.1.20.23: Since we have been thus dishonoured by the gods in this sacrifice, I shall remove your arrogance together with your lives. ॥23॥
7.1.20.24: Having spoken thus, the enraged lord burned the sacrificial enclosure with its great pavilions by the fire of his eye, as Hara burned the three cities. ॥24॥
7.1.20.25: Then all the lords of the Gaṇas, with bodies towering like mountains, uprooted the sacrificial posts and tied them with ropes to the necks of the hotṛ priests; ॥25॥
7.1.20.26: breaking the ornate sacrificial vessels and grinding them to powder in the water, and seizing the sacrificial implements, they hurled them into the current of the Gaṅgā. ॥26॥
7.1.20.27: There were heaps of divine food and drink like mountains, rivers of milk flowing with nectar, with mud of rich, thick curd; ॥27॥
7.1.20.28: meats of every kind, fragrant eatables, flavourful drinks, and things to lick and to suck. ॥28॥
7.1.20.29: The heroes devoured it with their mouths, plundered it and scattered it. With thunderbolts, discs, great tridents, spears, nooses and paṭṭiśas, ॥29॥
7.1.20.30: with pestles, swords, chisels, bhindipālas and axes, they struck all the arrogant gods headed by the guardians of the worlds. ॥30॥
7.1.20.31: The mighty heroes born from Vīrabhadra's body pierced them, with cries of cut, pierce, throw quickly, let them be killed, let them be torn apart, ॥31॥
7.1.20.32: Seize, strike, split, uproot — such cruel cries born of fury, piercing the ears like spikes, ॥32॥
7.1.20.33: befitting battle, arose here and there from the lords of the Gaṇas. Some, with rolling eyes, bit their lips with their fangs, showing their palates; ॥33॥
7.1.20.34: dragging out the ascetics staying in the hermitages, they killed them, carrying off the ladles and throwing the fire into the waters. ॥34॥
7.1.20.35: Breaking even the pitchers, smashing the jewelled altars, singing, roaring and laughing again and again, and drinking blood as liquor, the foremost Gaṇas danced. ॥35॥
7.1.20.36: Having crushed the immortals together with Indra, the Gaṇa lords — with the strength of mighty bulls, great elephants and lions, and of matchless power — performed many antics that made the hair bristle with excitement. ॥36॥
7.1.20.37: Some rejoiced, some struck, some ran, some babbled, ॥37॥
7.1.20.38: some danced, some laughed aloud, some Pramathas leapt about with vigour. ॥38॥
7.1.20.39: Some tried to seize the water-laden clouds; some leapt up to grab the sun; some terrible Pramathas, standing in the sky, wished to rush along with the wind. ॥39॥
7.1.20.40: And some, resembling mountain peaks, snatching away the gods' excellent weapons as Garuḍas snatch great serpents, roamed through the sphere of the sky, putting even the gods to flight. ॥40॥
7.1.20.41: Some Pramathas, looking like dark rain-clouds, tore up house after house, with their lattices, windows and raised platforms, flung them again and again into the middle of the water, and roared. ॥41॥
7.1.20.42: With its doors, door-panels and walls overturned, and its halls, roof-turrets and windows destroyed, alas, the sacrificial enclosure was shattered, like the untrue word of an untrustworthy person. ॥42॥
7.1.20.43: As the houses were being torn up, the women raised many helpless cries: Ah, lord! Father! O son of my father, O my brother, Mother, Uncle. ॥43॥
7.1.20.iti: Thus ends the twentieth adhyāya, named The destruction of the sacrifice, in the Pūrva-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥20॥
7.1.21.1: Vāyu said: Then all those chiefs of the gods, led by Viṣṇu and Śakra, terrified by fear and overwhelmed with fright, ran away. ॥1॥
7.1.21.2: Seeing the gods fleeing with their own limbs still unharmed, and thinking that those who deserved punishment had gone unpunished, the bull among the gaṇas grew angry. ॥2॥
7.1.21.3: Then, taking up his trident, the destroyer of foes by the power of Śarva, the mighty-armed one, with gaze turned upward and emitting flames from his mouth, ॥3॥
7.1.21.4: rushed even upon the immortals, as a lion upon elephants. As he charged at them, his gait, most charming, ॥4॥
7.1.21.5: like that of a rutting elephant, became a sight worth beholding. Then the mighty one agitated that great army of the gods, ॥5॥
7.1.21.6: as a rutting leader of an elephant herd churns a great lake. Assuming many colours—blue, pale white and red— ॥6॥
7.1.21.7: wearing as garment a tiger-skin studded with excellent golden stars, cutting, piercing, thrusting, drenching in blood, tearing apart and crushing, ॥7॥
7.1.21.8: Bhadra roamed among the hosts of gods like fire moving through dry brush. Him, the trident-bearer, moving here and there with great speed, ॥8॥
7.1.21.9: though he was one, all the gods thought to be a thousand. And Bhadrakālī, furious and frenzied with the intoxication swelling in battle, ॥9॥
7.1.21.10: pierced the gods in battle with her trident that shot forth flames. Bhadra, born of Rudra's wrath, shone by her side, ॥10॥
7.1.21.11: like the fire at the end of the age with its flickering, smoke-grey radiance. Bhadrakālī then, having put the gods to flight in battle, shone ॥11॥
7.1.21.12: like the flame of Śeṣa's fire at the end of the kalpa that has burnt up the whole world. Then the foremost of Rudra's gaṇas struck the Sun together with his horses, and the Rudras— ॥12॥
7.1.21.13: Bhadra swiftly struck the Sun on the head with his left foot, in sport. Bhadra struck Pāvaka (Agni) with swords, and Yama and Yamī with spears, ॥13॥
7.1.21.14: the Rudras with a firm trident, Varuṇa with strong maces, Nirṛti with iron clubs, and Vāyu—he himself, bearing a chisel-axe—with chisel-axes; ॥14॥
7.1.21.15: the heroic lord of the gaṇas, as if in sport, at once pierced in battle all the hosts of gods and the sages hostile to Śambhu. ॥15॥
7.1.21.16: Then the god cut off the lovely tip of Sarasvatī's nose with the tip of his fingernail, and likewise that of the mother of the gods. ॥16॥
7.1.21.17: With an axe he cut off the staff-like arm of Vibhāvasu (Agni), and lopped off two finger-breadths from the front of his tongue, which had received the oblations. ॥17॥
7.1.21.18: Likewise the god cut off with his fingernail-tip the right nostril of the goddess Svāhā and her left nipple. ॥18॥
7.1.21.19: Bhadra, of supreme speed, forcibly tore out Bhaga's large eyes, radiant like lotuses. ॥19॥
7.1.21.20: And he struck Pūṣan's row of teeth, gleaming like a string of pearls, with the tip of his bow; by that Pūṣan became indistinct of speech. ॥20॥
7.1.21.21: Then the god, in sport, pressed down the Moon with his big toe for a moment like a worm and rubbed him on the ground. ॥21॥
7.1.21.22: In supreme wrath Bhadra cut off Dakṣa's head, and while his hostile wife was still wailing, he gave it to Bhadrakālī. ॥22॥
7.1.21.23: Delighted, the goddess took that head, which resembled a palmyra fruit, and played a game of ball with it on the battlefield. ॥23॥
7.1.21.24: Then the women of Dakṣa's sacrifice were beaten with feet and hands by the lords of the gaṇas, as a wanton woman is by her husbands. ॥24॥
7.1.21.25: Ariṣṭanemi, Soma, Dharma and the Prajāpati, Bahuputra, Āṅgirasa, Kṛśāśva and Kāśyapa— ॥25॥
7.1.21.26: seizing them by the neck, the mighty gaṇa chiefs, valourous as lions, reviling them harshly with words, struck them on the head with their fists. ॥26॥
7.1.21.27: Their wives and their sons' wives were assaulted by bhūtas and vetālas, as in the Kali age women of good families are by paramours through force. ॥27॥
7.1.21.28: And that sacrificial enclosure—its pitchers smashed, its sacrificial posts broken, its festivity gone, its great halls set ablaze, its gates and arches shattered, ॥28॥
7.1.21.29: its army of gods uprooted, its ascetics being slain, the sound of Vedic chanting stilled, its gathering of people depleted, ॥29॥
7.1.21.30: its distressed women crying, all its equipment destroyed—that tormented sacrificial ground then became like a desolate forest. ॥30॥
7.1.21.31: Shattered by the force of the trident, with arms, thighs and chests split, and with heads severed, the best of the gods fell upon the earth. ॥31॥
7.1.21.32: When those gods had been slain and had fallen by the thousands, the lord of the gaṇas in an instant entered the āhavanīya fire. ॥32॥
7.1.21.33: Then, seeing Bhadra, resembling the fire of doomsday, entered there, Yajña, afraid of death, assumed the form of a deer and fled. ॥33॥
7.1.21.34: Bhadra, drawing his great bow, terrifying with the twang of its strong string, rushed after him, shooting arrows all the while. ॥34॥
7.1.21.35: Drawing to the full, up to his ear, the bow that looked like a raincloud, he twanged its string and made heaven, sky and earth resound on every side. ॥35॥
7.1.21.36: Hearing that roar, Yajña was distraught, thinking, I am slain. With a curved half-moon arrow the hero struck the Person of the Sacrifice— ॥36॥
7.1.21.37: whose feet stumbled from great fear, trembling, his lustre gone, running in the form of a deer—and then made him headless. ॥37॥
7.1.21.38: Seeing him, sprung from the Sun, thus humiliated, Viṣṇu, supremely enraged, made ready for battle. ॥38॥
7.1.21.39: Garuḍa, king of all birds and eater of serpents, carried him at great speed on his shoulder with its joints bent. ॥39॥
7.1.21.40: And those gods who were left over from the slaughter, led by the king of the gods, gave him their support, as if ready to give up their lives. ॥40॥
7.1.21.41: Seeing the gods together with Viṣṇu, as a lion sees jackals, the lord of the Bhūtas laughed, untroubled, like a lion. ॥41॥
7.1.21.iti: Thus ends the twenty-first adhyāya, named The punishment of the gods, in the Pūrva-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥21॥
7.1.22.1: Vāyu said: At that moment a chariot appeared in the sky, shining like a thousand suns, with a bull-banner of beautiful cloth. ॥1॥
7.1.22.2: It was magnificent with a pair of jewel-like horses, had four chariot-wheels, and was adorned with many stored divine missiles, weapons and gems. ॥2॥
7.1.22.3: The charioteer of that excellent chariot, too, was the very one who had formerly stood on Śarva's chariot in the battle against Tripura. ॥3॥
7.1.22.4: That Brahmā, at the very command of the trident-bearer, brought that excellent chariot near Hari on the battlefield and, with joined palms, spoke. ॥4॥
7.1.22.5: O lord Bhadra, of auspicious form, the blessed, moon-adorned, imperishable hero commands you to mount the chariot. ॥5॥
7.1.22.6: Tryambaka, staying near Raibhya's hermitage together with Ambikā, is watching your irresistible valour, O mighty-armed one. ॥6॥
7.1.22.7: Hearing those words of his, that hero, the elephant among the gaṇas, favouring the Grandsire, mounted the divine chariot. ॥7॥
7.1.22.8: When he was thus on that excellent chariot with Brahmā as charioteer, Bhadra's splendour grew, like that of Rudra, the enemy of the cities. ॥8॥
7.1.22.9: Then the mighty Bhānukampa, placing at his mouth an excellent blazing conch shining like the full moon, blew it. ॥9॥
7.1.22.10: Hearing that sound of the conch, like that of a bursting ocean, the fire in the bellies of the gods blazed up out of fear. ॥10॥
7.1.22.11: In an instant the directions, along with the hollows of the sky, became crowded with Yakṣas, Vidyādharas, serpent-lords and Siddhas eager to see the battle. ॥11॥
7.1.22.12: Then that Nārāyaṇa-cloud, with the Śārṅga loosing arrows from the curve of the bow as a cloud does from its rainbow, struck the bull among the gaṇas with a great shower of arrows. ॥12॥
7.1.22.13: Seeing Viṣṇu coming on, raining arrows a hundredfold, Bhadra, who could release a thousand arrows, took up his victorious bow. ॥13॥
7.1.22.14: Taking up that divine bow, terrible in battle, he slowly drew it, as the Lord drew Meru as his bow. ॥14॥
7.1.22.15: As that bow was being drawn there arose a mighty sound; with that great sound it made the earth tremble. ॥15॥
7.1.22.16: Then the glorious lord of the gaṇas, of fierce valour, himself seized an excellent, terrible, blazing arrow like a venomous serpent. ॥16॥
7.1.22.17: As he drew out the arrow, his arm, joined to the mouth of the quiver, looked like a serpent about to enter an anthill. ॥17॥
7.1.22.18: Drawn out into his hand, the arrow at that moment shone like a young snake caught in the jaws of a great serpent. ॥18॥
7.1.22.19: Enraged, Bhadra, of Rudra's valour, deeply pierced the imperishable Viṣṇu on the forehead with a dense, sharp arrow. ॥19॥
7.1.22.20: Struck on the forehead, and already humiliated before, Viṣṇu grew angry at the lord of the gaṇas, as a bull at a lion. ॥20॥
7.1.22.21: Then, with a great thunderbolt-like arrow with a cruel tip, he pierced the king of the gaṇas in his serpent-like arm. ॥21॥
7.1.22.22: The mighty Vīrabhadra in turn swiftly shot into his arm again an arrow bright as ten thousand suns. ॥22॥
7.1.22.23: Viṣṇu struck Bhadra again, and Bhadra likewise Viṣṇu again; he struck him and he struck him — so, O brahmins, the two kept striking each other with arrows. ॥23॥
7.1.22.24: As the two swiftly released arrows at each other, a tumultuous, hair-raising battle arose between them. ॥24॥
7.1.22.25: Seeing that tumultuous battle between the two, a great cry of alarm raised by the sky-dwellers arose in the heavens. ॥25॥
7.1.22.26: Then, with a fire-tipped arrow bright as the sun, Bhadra pierced him very firmly in Viṣṇu's broad chest. ॥26॥
7.1.22.27: Struck hard by that arrow of fierce impact, he felt great pain and fell down unconscious. ॥27॥
7.1.22.28: Then, rising again as if after a moment, Hari regained consciousness and hurled all his divine missiles back at him. ॥28॥
7.1.22.29: And he, the commander of Śarva's army, suddenly warded off with terrible counter-arrows all the arrows released from Viṣṇu's bow. ॥29॥
7.1.22.30: Then Viṣṇu, eyes red with anger, released at that lord of the gaṇas an arrow marked with his own name, never obstructed anywhere. That arrow, with his excellent arrow named Bhadra, Bhadra — ॥30॥
7.1.22.31: — the lord cut into a hundred pieces on its path before it reached him. Then with one arrow he cut the Śārṅga, and with two the wings of Garuḍa, ॥31॥
7.1.22.32: he cut in the twinkling of an eye; it was like a marvel. Then Viṣṇu, through the power of yoga, from his body very terrible gods — ॥32॥
7.1.22.33: bearing conch, discus and mace in their hands — he sent forth by thousands. All of them, in a mere instant, as Śaṅkara burned the Tripura-demons, ॥33॥
7.1.22.34: the mighty-armed one burned up with fire produced from his eye. Then Viṣṇu, more enraged, swiftly raising his discus, ॥34॥
7.1.22.35: was then ready to hurl it at that hero. Seeing him standing before him with discus raised, ॥35॥
7.1.22.36: the lord of the gaṇas, as if smiling, paralysed him without effort. With his limbs paralysed, that terrible discus, unmatched anywhere, ॥36॥
7.1.22.37: Viṣṇu, though wishing to hurl it, was not able. As if gasping, holding up one arm bearing the discus, ॥37॥
7.1.22.38: he stood, become inert, motionless as a stone — like a soul without a body, or a bull without horns, ॥38॥
7.1.22.39: or a lion without fangs — so Viṣṇu stood. Seeing Viṣṇu fallen into that sorry state, the gods led by Indra, roused against the lord of the gaṇas like bulls against a lion, ॥39॥
7.1.22.40: took up their weapons and, enraged, came forward to fight. Seeing them in battle, Bhadra, as a lion sees petty beasts, ॥40॥
7.1.22.41: The blameless hero, Rudra's very own body, surrounded by excellent heroic gaṇas, paralysed the gods with a terrible loud laugh. ॥41॥
7.1.22.42: Likewise the right hand of Indra, the god of a hundred sacrifices, holding the thunderbolt, as he was about to hurl it with the thunderbolt raised, became as if painted motionless. ॥42॥
7.1.22.43: The arms of all the others too, though full of vigour, likewise fell back, like the undertakings of the lazy. ॥43॥
