7.1.32.21: From his grace comes the supreme yoga that makes Śiva directly perceived; through the direct perception of Śiva one is freed from the cause of saṃsāra. ॥21॥
7.1.32.22: Then he becomes free of saṃsāra; liberated, he becomes equal to Śiva. This is the means taught by Brahmā; that very means is now explained separately. ॥22॥
7.1.32.23: Śiva, Maheśvara, Rudra, Viṣṇu, Pitāmaha, Saṃsāravaidya (physician of worldly existence), Sarvajña (the omniscient) and Paramātman — these are the principal ones. ॥23॥
7.1.32.24: This principal group of eight names designates Śiva; the first five should be understood as corresponding in order to Śāntyatītā and the rest. ॥24॥
7.1.32.25: These are the names of Sadāśiva and the others, owing to their assumption of the five limiting adjuncts; but when the adjuncts cease, each name ceases accordingly. ॥25॥
7.1.32.26: For the position (pada) itself is eternal, while the holders of positions are regarded as non-eternal, since when the positions change, the holders are released. ॥26॥
7.1.32.27: In another cycle, the attainment of that position by others is spoken of again; thus the first group of five names would denote other selves. ॥27॥
7.1.32.28: But the other three names, through their connection with the material cause and the rest, and because they express threefold adjuncts, continue to apply to Śiva alone. ॥28॥
7.1.32.29: Because contact with beginningless impurity is by nature absent in him from the very outset, he is the utterly pure Self; hence he is called Śiva. ॥29॥
7.1.32.30: Or else, the Lord, sole treasure of all auspicious qualities, is called Śiva by the wise who expound the meaning of the Śiva-principle. ॥30॥
7.1.32.31: Prakṛti is held to be beyond the twenty-three tattvas; and beyond Prakṛti they declare the Puruṣa, the twenty-fifth. ॥31॥
7.1.32.32: He whom they call the syllable (svara, Oṃ) at the beginning of the Veda, through the relation of denoted and denoter; and since his true nature is knowable through the Veda alone, he is established in the Vedānta. ॥32॥
7.1.32.33: He who is beyond that Puruṣa merged in Prakṛti is Maheśvara, because the activity of both Prakṛti and Puruṣa depends on him. ॥33॥
7.1.32.34: Or else, this imperishable principle of three guṇas is to be accepted as Prakṛti; one should know Māyā as Prakṛti, and Maheśvara as the wielder of Māyā. ॥34॥
7.1.32.35: The agitator of Māyā, the infinite one, through his union with Maheśvara, is proclaimed as the Self of Time, the supreme Self and so on, both gross and subtle. ॥35॥
7.1.32.36: Rud means sorrow or the cause of sorrow; because the Lord drives that away from us, Śiva, the supreme cause, is called Rudra by the wise. ॥36॥
7.1.32.37: Unwearied, Śiva pervades and presides over everything from the tattvas down to the elements, in bodies and the rest; therefore he is Rudra, present everywhere. ॥37॥
7.1.32.38: Since Śiva is the father even of those embodied beings who are the fathers of the world, he is declared Pitāmaha (grandfather) because of his fatherhood toward all. ॥38॥
7.1.32.39: Just as a physician who knows the root cause removes a disease by remedies and medicines, so likewise, through dissolution, enjoyment and office (laya, bhoga, adhikāra), ॥39॥
7.1.32.40: the Lord is always the remover of saṃsāra together with its root; hence he is called Saṃsāravaidya by those who know the meaning of all the tattvas. ॥40॥
7.1.32.41: Even though these senses exist for the purpose of attaining knowledge of the ten objects, bound souls do not know completely the things that occur in the three times, both gross and subtle. ॥41॥
7.1.32.42: The bound souls, covered with impurity (mala) by māyā itself, do not know them. But even when all the means of knowing every object are absent, ॥42॥
7.1.32.43: Sadāśiva knows effortlessly each thing exactly as it stands; therefore he is called omniscient. ॥43॥
7.1.32.44: Because of his eternal union with these supreme qualities he is the Self of all; and since there is no supreme self apart from himself, Śiva himself is the Supreme Self. ॥44॥
7.1.32.45: Having received this octad of names through the grace of the preceptor, one should cut the knot of the kalās beginning with Nivṛtti by means of the five names beginning with Śiva, ॥45॥
7.1.32.46: cutting them each in its proper way and in due order, and purifying them according to their qualities, with names/breaths repeated together with upward impulse (udghāta), or else with restrained breath; ॥46॥
7.1.32.47: having pierced the path furnished with the heart, throat, palate, the point between the brows and the brahmarandhra, and leading one's own self, in the form of the puryaṣṭaka, through the suṣumnā ॥47॥
7.1.32.48: having led it above the moon located at the dvādaśānta, into the radiance of Śiva, and having withdrawn the face of outward activity, then, through dissolution, according to the proper purification, ॥48॥
7.1.32.49: and when the body has again been drenched by the shower of nectar of Śakti, bringing one's own self, having the form of a nectar-self, down into the heart, ॥49॥
7.1.32.50: and meditating on Mahādeva Śaṅkara, loving towards his devotees, seated on a white lotus beyond the moon located at the dvādaśānta, ॥50॥
7.1.32.51: the god as Ardhanārīśvara, stainless, of charming form, resembling pure crystal, gracious, of cool radiance — ॥51॥
7.1.32.52: having meditated on the god in the mind, the man, with a composed mind, should then worship him with flowers of devotion, using the octad of Śiva's names alone. ॥52॥
7.1.32.53: At the end of the worship, the man, again restraining his breaths and concentrating his mind properly, should recite the octad of names of Śarva. ॥53॥
7.1.32.54: Having offered eight oblations in the navel, then concluding with the full oblation and a salutation, and having performed the final worship by offering eight flowers, ॥54॥
7.1.32.55: he should offer his own self by means of a palmful of water. Having done so, very soon he obtains the auspicious Pāśupata knowledge, ॥55॥
7.1.32.56: he obtains it, and firm establishment in it, and likewise unsurpassed conduct; and having attained the supreme yoga, he is liberated — of this there is no doubt. ॥56॥
7.1.32.iti: Thus ends the thirty-second adhyāya, named The best practice, in the Pūrva-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥32॥
7.1.33.1: The sages said: O lord, we wish to hear about the supreme Pāśupata vow, by performing which even Brahmā and the others are all known as Pāśupatas. ॥1॥
7.1.33.2: Vāyu said: I shall declare to you the secret Pāśupata vow, which cuts away all sins, a Vedic rite heard in the Atharvaśiras. ॥2॥
7.1.33.3: The time is the full-moon day of Caitra; the place is one that belongs to Śiva, or a holy field, a garden and the like, or a forest—any place that is commendable and of auspicious marks. ॥3॥
7.1.33.4: There, first, on the thirteenth lunar day, having bathed well and duly performed the daily rites, having taken leave of his own teacher, worshipped him and bowed to him, ॥4॥
7.1.33.5: having performed a special worship, himself wearing white garments, with a white sacred thread, and with white garlands and unguents, ॥5॥
7.1.33.6: seated on a seat of darbha grass, holding a handful of darbha, having done three breath-controls, facing east or north, and having meditated on the God and the Goddess by way of informing them of his intent, ॥6॥
7.1.33.7: he should become consecrated, resolving, I undertake this vow—either until the fall of the body, or for twelve years, ॥7॥
7.1.33.8: or half of that, or half of that again, or for twelve months, or half of that, or half of that again, or for a single month, ॥8॥
7.1.33.9: or for twelve days, or for six days, or half of that, or a single day—as the limit of the vow's resolution. ॥9॥
7.1.33.10: Having duly installed the fire for the purpose of the Virajā oblation, and having offered with ghee, with fuel-sticks and with caru in due order, ॥10॥
7.1.33.11: and having filled up that full oblation, he should again offer with the root mantra, using those same fuel-sticks and other materials, intending the purification of the principles (tattvas), ॥11॥
7.1.33.12: recollecting, may these principles in my body be purified: the five elements, the subtle elements, and the five organs of action, ॥12॥
7.1.33.13: the senses divided as those of knowledge and of action, by the division of five functions; the seven bodily constituents beginning with skin; the five vital airs beginning with prāṇa; ॥13॥
7.1.33.14: mind, intellect, ego-sense, the guṇas, Prakṛti and Puruṣa, Rāga, Vidyā and Kalā, Niyati and Kāla, ॥14॥
7.1.33.15: Māyā and Śuddhavidyā, Maheśvara and Sadāśiva, Śakti and the Śiva-principle—these, in order, they know as the principles. ॥15॥
7.1.33.16: Having offered with the Virajā mantras, this offerer becomes free of impurity (virajā); obtaining Śiva's grace, he indeed becomes possessed of knowledge. ॥16॥
7.1.33.17: Then, taking cow-dung, forming it into a ball, consecrating it with mantras, placing it in the fire and sprinkling it, on that day he should eat only sacrificial food. ॥17॥
7.1.33.18: At dawn on the fourteenth day, having done all that was described before, he should remain fasting that day and pass the remaining time. ॥18॥
7.1.33.19: In the morning on the festival (full-moon) day, having done likewise up to the end of the oblation, he should withdraw the Rudra-fire and carefully collect the ash. ॥19॥
7.1.33.20: Then, becoming one with matted hair, or shaven-headed, or with a single matted lock as a tuft, he should bathe; then, if he is free of shame, he may be sky-clad (naked). ॥20॥
7.1.33.21: Or he may wear ochre cloth, or garments of hide or rags, or a single cloth, or bark; and he should carry a staff and wear a girdle. ॥21॥
7.1.33.22: Afterwards, having washed his feet and sipped water twice, he should gather that ash produced from the Virajā fire for his own body, ॥22॥
7.1.33.23: and with the six Atharvan mantras beginning agniḥ, in order, having wiped the limbs from the head down to the feet, he should touch them with that ash. ॥23॥
7.1.33.24: Then, in the same order, taking up the ash, he should smear all his limbs with it, using the praṇava or the Śiva mantra. ॥24॥
7.1.33.25: Then he should make the tripuṇḍra, called tryāyuṣa; having attained the state of Śiva, he should then practise Śiva-yoga. ॥25॥
7.1.33.26: He should perform this Pāśupata vow in this way at the three junctures of the day; it grants enjoyment and liberation and removes the state of being a bound soul (paśutva). ॥26॥
7.1.33.27: Having cast off that paśu-state by performing the Pāśupata vow, the eternal Mahādeva in the form of the liṅga is to be worshipped. ॥27॥
7.1.33.28: He should arrange as a seat a golden eight-petalled lotus adorned with the nine gems, furnished with pericarp and filaments, ॥28॥
7.1.33.29: this if he has wealth; in its absence, a red or white lotus; and in the absence of that too, one made purely of mental conception. ॥29॥
7.1.33.30: Placing in the middle of that lotus's pericarp a small crystal liṅga with a pedestal, he should worship it duly and in order. ॥30॥
7.1.33.31: Having installed that purified liṅga according to rule, and having conceived the seat and the form in the manner of the five-faced Śiva, ॥31॥
7.1.33.32: he should bathe it with full golden pitchers filled with the five cow-products and other things, gathered according to his means. ॥32॥
7.1.33.33: Having anointed the liṅga together with its altar with fragrant substances, with camphor, sandal and the like, and saffron, and having adorned it with ornaments, ॥33॥
7.1.33.34: with bilva leaves, with lotuses, with red and white water-lilies, with blue lilies, and with various other fragrant flowers, ॥34॥
7.1.33.35: with holy, excellent and variegated leaves, with dūrvā grass, unbroken rice and the like—having worshipped as available, according to the procedure of the great worship, ॥35॥
7.1.33.36: he should present incense, lamp and food-offering; and having offered them, if he has means, he should also perform the auspicious festive rite. ॥36॥
7.1.33.37: All substances that are desired, excellent and justly earned should be offered, especially in this vow. ॥37॥
7.1.33.38: The number of bilva leaves, water-lilies and lotuses is held to be a thousand each; the alternative number, O twice-born, is one hundred and eight. ॥38॥
7.1.33.39: Even there, he should especially not omit the bilva leaf. They say one golden lotus is superior to a thousand lotuses. ॥39॥
7.1.33.40: For blue lilies and the rest too, this rule is the same as for bilva leaves. For other flowers there is no fixed rule; he should offer as available. ॥40॥
7.1.33.41: The eightfold arghya is the finest offering; incense and unguent are offered specifically to each face: sandal-paste on the face called Vāmadeva, and yellow orpiment on Tatpuruṣa, ॥41॥
7.1.33.42: and ashes on Īśāna. Some regard such things as unguent and not as incense, since a separate incense is prescribed. White aloe-wood is offered on the face called Aghora, and black aloe-wood further, ॥42॥
7.1.33.43: guggulu on Tatpuruṣa, saugandhika on Sadyojāta, the gentle face, and on Īśāna uśīra and the like — one should offer incense in this specific way. ॥43॥
7.1.33.44: Incense mixed with sugar, honey, camphor and ghee of a tawny cow, made of sandal, aloe-wood and other woods, is called the general incense. ॥44॥
7.1.33.45: Then a row of lamps with camphor wicks, rich in ghee, should be offered; after that arghya and sipping-water should be offered to each face. ॥45॥
7.1.33.46: In the first enclosure Heramba and Ṣaṇmukha are to be worshipped in order; and then, in the first enclosure, the Brahma-limbs are worshipped. ॥46॥
7.1.33.47: In the second enclosure the Vighneśas, the Cakravartins, are to be worshipped; in the third enclosure the eight forms beginning with Bhava are to be worshipped. ॥47॥
7.1.33.48: There also are worshipped the eleven forms beginning with Mahādeva; in the fourth enclosure all the lords of the gaṇas are to be worshipped. ॥48॥
7.1.33.49: Outside the lotus, in the fifth enclosure, in order, the regents of the ten directions are to be worshipped, together with their weapons and their attendants; ॥49॥
7.1.33.50: the mind-born sons of Brahmā, all the hosts of luminaries, all the goddesses and gods, and all, all the sky-goers, ॥50॥
7.1.33.51: and others dwelling in Pātāla, all the hosts of sages too, the yogins, all the sacrifices, the birds, and likewise the Mothers, ॥51॥
7.1.33.52: and the Kṣetrapālas with their hosts — all this moving and unmoving world is to be worshipped out of love for Śiva, regarding it as endowed with Śambhu's glory. ॥52॥
7.1.33.53: Then, at the end of the enclosure-worship, having worshipped the Supreme Lord, one should offer with devotion a delightful oblation-food with ghee, together with a fan. ॥53॥
7.1.33.54: Having given mouth-fresheners and the like, and betel with its accompaniments, and having adorned the Lord again with ornaments of various flowers, ॥54॥
7.1.33.55: at the end of the waving of lights, one should elaborate and complete the rest of the worship, and offer a cup with its accessories and a bed. ॥55॥
7.1.33.56: One should offer a moon-like necklace and a couch — all that is excellent, fit for a king and delightful, according to one's means. ॥56॥
7.1.33.57: Having done this and had it done, having made the fire-offering and the counter-worship, and having recited the Vyomeśa hymn, one should recite the five-syllable vidyā. ॥57॥
7.1.33.58: Having made circumambulation and prostration, one should surrender oneself; then, in front of the deity, one should worship the guru and a brahmin. ॥58॥
7.1.33.59: Having given arghya and eight flowers, having dismissed the deity from the liṅga, and having withdrawn the fire into one's own fire and dismissed it as well, ॥59॥
7.1.33.60: a person should perform daily the service described above in this way. Then that liṅga with its lotus, together with all the accessories, ॥60॥
7.1.33.61: one should offer to one's own guru or install in a Śiva temple. And having worshipped the gurus, the brahmins, and especially the vow-observers, ॥61॥
7.1.33.62: if able, one should gratify devotees, the twice-born, and the poor and helpless. He himself, if able, should keep a fast, or eat fruits and roots, ॥62॥
7.1.33.63: or live on milk, or eat alms, or eat once a day; eating at night, always taking moderate food, keeping to sleeping on the ground, pure, ॥63॥
7.1.33.64: sleeping on ashes or on grass, or wearing bark-cloth and deerskin, ever under the vow of celibacy — so one should observe this vow. ॥64॥
7.1.33.65: On Sunday, on the day of Ārdrā, on the fifteenth day of both fortnights, and on the eighth and fourteenth, one who is able should also fast. ॥65॥
7.1.33.66: With every effort one should avoid, in mind, deed and speech, heretics, the fallen, menstruating women, those in birth-impurity, outcastes and the like. ॥66॥
7.1.33.67: One should always be given to forbearance, generosity, compassion, truth and non-violence, content and tranquil, and devoted to japa and meditation. ॥67॥
7.1.33.68: One should bathe at the three junctures of the day, or else take an ash-bath, and perform the special worship with mind, words and speech. ॥68॥
7.1.33.69: What need to say more here? The vow-observer should do nothing inauspicious. But if through carelessness he acts so, he should weigh its gravity or lightness, ॥69॥
7.1.33.70: and perform suitable expiation through worship, fire-offering, japa and the like. Thus he should conduct himself until the completion of the vow, not carelessly. ॥70॥
7.1.33.71: He should make a gift of a cow, release a bull, and perform worship with all his wealth — a devotee, for the pleasure of Śiva, free of all desires. ॥71॥
7.1.33.72: This general procedure of this vow has been told in brief; I shall now declare the special rules for each month, as I have heard. ॥72॥
7.1.33.73: In Vaiśākha the liṅga is to be of diamond; in Jyeṣṭha an auspicious one of emerald; in Āṣāḍha one should know it to be of pearl; in Śrāvaṇa made of sapphire; ॥73॥
7.1.33.74: and in the month of Bhādrapada an excellent one made of ruby; in the month of Āśvina one should know the liṅga to be a fine one of gomedaka (hessonite). ॥74॥
7.1.33.75: In Kārttika a liṅga of coral; in Mārgaśīrṣa of cat's-eye; in Pauṣa made of topaz; and in Māgha of sun-stone; ॥75॥
7.1.33.76: in Phālguna one made of moonstone; in Caitra the interchange of these, or else; in all months, if gems are not obtainable, one of gold; ॥76॥
7.1.33.77: in the absence of gold, one of silver, or of copper, or likewise of stone, or of clay as available, or of lac, or of some other material, ॥77॥
7.1.33.78: or one may make a liṅga composed of all fragrant substances, as one likes. At the time of the vow's conclusion, having performed the daily rites, ॥78॥
7.1.33.79: having performed the special worship and made the fire-offering just as before, and having likewise worshipped the teacher and especially the vow-observers, ॥79॥
7.1.33.80: permitted also by the preceptor, facing east or north, seated on darbha grass with darbha in hand, and restraining the prāṇa and apāna breaths, ॥80॥
7.1.33.81: Having repeated the root mantra according to his capacity, having meditated on the three-eyed One together with Ambā, having taken leave as before and bowed with joined palms, ॥81॥
7.1.33.82: saying, O Lord, by your command I relinquish this vow, he should then cast away to the north the darbha grass placed at the base of the liṅga. ॥82॥
7.1.33.83: Then he should also give up the staff, matted hair, bark garment and girdle. Having again sipped water according to rule, he should utter the five-syllabled mantra. ॥83॥
7.1.33.84: He who, having taken the lifelong initiation, undisturbed, performs this vow until the end of his body, is indeed known as a naiṣṭhika lifelong observer. ॥84॥
7.1.33.85: He should be known as one beyond the stages of life (atyāśramī) and likewise as a great Pāśupata; he alone is the best of ascetics, and he alone is a great vow-keeper. ॥85॥
7.1.33.86: Among seekers of liberation there is none equal to him, who has fulfilled his duty. The ascetic who has become a naiṣṭhika they call the foremost of naiṣṭhikas. ॥86॥
7.1.33.87: He who performs this vow daily, or for twelve days, he too becomes equal to a naiṣṭhika, owing to his connection with an intense vow. ॥87॥
7.1.33.88: He who, devoted to vows and anointed with ghee, performs this vow even for two, three or one day, he too is a naiṣṭhika of a kind. ॥88॥
7.1.33.89: He who, free from desire, performs this supreme vow simply as a duty, with his self ever offered to Śiva — none anywhere is equal to him. ॥89॥
7.1.33.90: A learned twice-born covered with ash is at once freed from the most terrible sins arising from great crimes; there is no doubt of this. ॥90॥
7.1.33.91: The supreme potency of Rudra's fire is proclaimed to be ash. Therefore one endowed with ash is at all times potent. ॥91॥
7.1.33.92: The faults of one devoted to ash perish through contact with the fire of ash. One whose self is purified by ash-bathing is known as bhasmaniṣṭha, devoted to ash. ॥92॥
7.1.33.93: A man whose whole body is smeared with ash, who shines with ash and bears the tripuṇḍra, and who bathes in ash, is known as bhasmaniṣṭha. ॥93॥
7.1.33.94: Ghosts, spirits, piśācas and exceedingly unbearable diseases flee from the presence of one devoted to ash; there is no doubt. ॥94॥
7.1.33.95: It is called bhasita from its shining (bhāsana), bhasma from its devouring (bhakṣaṇa) of impurity; bhūti because it brings prosperity (bhūti), and rakṣā because it gives supreme protection (rakṣā). ॥95॥
7.1.33.96: What more need be said here as the reason for the greatness of ash? The god Maheśvara himself, as a vow-keeper, bathed in ash. ॥96॥
7.1.33.97: This ash belonging to the Supreme Lord is the supreme weapon of the Śaivas, by which the calamities in the austerity of Dhaumya's elder brother were warded off. ॥97॥
7.1.33.98: Therefore, having performed the Pāśupata vow with every effort, and gathering ash as one would wealth, one should be devoted to bathing in ash. ॥98॥
7.1.33.iti: Thus ends the thirty-third adhyāya, named The procedure of the vow of Paśupati, in the Pūrva-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥33॥
7.1.34.1: The sages said: The child, Dhaumya's elder brother, performed austerity for the sake of milk, and for that reason the god who bears the trident gave him the ocean of milk. ॥1॥
7.1.34.2: How did that little child come to be an expounder of the Śiva scriptures? And how did he come to know Śiva's true nature and become steadfast in austerity? ॥2॥
7.1.34.3: And how, having gained knowledge during his practice of austerity, did he obtain the ash, the supreme potency of Rudra's fire, as his own protection? ॥3॥
7.1.34.4: Vāyu said: This child who performed austerity was no ordinary one; he was the son of the wise Vyāghrapāda, the foremost of sages. ॥4॥
7.1.34.5: He had become perfected in a former birth; fallen from his own station for some reason, he had by good fortune been born as a sage's son. ॥5॥
7.1.34.6: His austerity, which sprang from a longing for milk, became the doorway to the grace of Mahādeva that was destined to come to him through good fortune. ॥6॥
7.1.34.7: Therefore Śaṅkara himself granted him lordship over all the gaṇas and eternal youth, together with the ocean of milk. ॥7॥
7.1.34.8: His acquisition of knowledge too came solely from Śaṅkara's grace; for the wise know the supreme Kaumāra knowledge to be directly full of śakti. ॥8॥
7.1.34.9: His being an expounder of the Śiva scriptures was also brought about by that grace, like Nandin, who obtained an ocean of knowledge from the mouths of Kumāra and Umā. ॥9॥
7.1.34.10: But the visible cause of his attaining knowledge of Śiva was, directly, his own mother's words, born of grief, on account of milk. ॥10॥
7.1.34.11: Once he drank a very little milk at his maternal uncle's hermitage; then with envy, seeing his uncle's son satisfied with excellent milk, ॥11॥
7.1.34.12: having seen his uncle's son standing there after drinking as much as he wanted, Upamanyu, son of Vyāghrapāda, spoke affectionately to his mother. ॥12॥
7.1.34.13: Upamanyu said: Mother, mother, O fortunate ascetic lady, give me cow's milk, very sweet and warm, and not a little; I will drink it. ॥13॥
7.1.34.14: Vāyu said: Hearing her son's words, his mother, the ascetic queen of Vyāghrapāda, was then grieved. ॥14॥
7.1.34.15: Fondling him with great love and embracing her son tenderly, she, sorrowful, then wept, remembering her own poverty. ॥15॥
7.1.34.16: Remembering the milk again and again, the radiant boy Upamanyu kept crying and said to her, give, give. ॥16॥
7.1.34.17: Recognising his stubbornness, the ascetic wife of the brāhmaṇa then devised a good means to calm that obstinacy. ॥17॥
7.1.34.18: Then, looking over the grains she herself had gathered by gleaning, the sweet-voiced woman mixed grain-flour with water, ॥18॥
7.1.34.19: and saying gently, come, come, my son, she, stricken with sorrow, embraced her son, took him up, and gave him the artificial milk. ॥19॥
7.1.34.20: Having drunk the artificial milk given by his mother, the boy, greatly distressed, said to his mother, this is not milk. ॥20॥
7.1.34.21: Then, grieved, she looked at him, kissed him on the head, wiped her son's lotus-like eyes with her hands, and said: ॥21॥
7.1.34.22: The mother said: Those rivers full of jewels, ranging through heaven and the netherworld, are not seen by the unfortunate, nor by those who lack devotion to Śiva. ॥22॥
7.1.34.23: Kingdom, heaven, liberation, food made from milk—these cherished things they do not obtain when Śiva is not pleased with them. ॥23॥
7.1.34.24: Everything is born of Bhava's grace, not of any other god's grace. Those devoted to other gods wander about, afflicted with sorrow. ॥24॥
7.1.34.25: So where would milk come from for us, who always live in the forest? Where are the means of getting milk, child, and where are we forest-dwellers? ॥25॥
7.1.34.26: Because of utter want and poverty, I, unfortunate as I am, gave you this false milk, made by mixing flour with water. ॥26॥
7.1.34.27: You drank a little sweet boiled milk at your uncle's house, and knowing the sweetness of what you drank, you keep remembering milk of that kind, ॥27॥
7.1.34.28: and by crying, this given to me is not milk, you grieve me. Without Śambhu's grace there is no milk for you. ॥28॥
7.1.34.29: Whatever is offered with devotion at the lotus feet of him, accompanied by Ambā and by his gaṇas, that is the cause of all prosperity. ॥29॥
7.1.34.30: Until now we have not worshipped Mahādeva, the giver of wealth, who grants to those with desires the fruits they desire, as declared. ॥30॥
7.1.34.31: Before this, we did not worship Śiva with wealth as our aim; therefore we have become poor, and therefore there is no milk for you. ॥31॥
7.1.34.32: Whatever was given in a former birth with Śiva as its object, O son, that alone is received—not otherwise, not what was given with Viṣṇu or another lord as its object. ॥32॥
7.1.34.33: Vāyu said: Hearing these truthful words of his mother, which betrayed her grief and more, the boy, though young, felt inward remorse and spoke these bold words. ॥33॥
7.1.34.34: Upamanyu said: Enough of grief from now on, mother. If Śaṅkara with Ambā exists, give up your grief, O fortunate one; all will be well. ॥34॥
7.1.34.35: Hear my words today, mother: if Mahādeva exists anywhere, then sooner or later I will obtain the ocean of milk. ॥35॥
7.1.34.36: Vāyu said: Hearing these words of the high-minded boy, his wise mother, greatly pleased, then replied. ॥36॥
7.1.34.37: The mother said: my dear, you have resolved well, and it increases my joy. Do not delay; worship Sadāśiva together with Ambā. ॥37॥
7.1.34.38: Śiva indeed is greater than all, the supreme cause. The whole world is made by him; Brahmā and the others are his servants. ॥38॥
7.1.34.39: Our sovereignty is wrought by his grace; we are servants of that lord. Apart from him we know no other—Śaṅkara, who brings welfare to the world. ॥39॥
7.1.34.40: Abandoning other gods in deed, mind and speech, worship him alone, together with Ambā and his gaṇas, with heartfelt devotion. ॥40॥
7.1.34.41: Of that God of gods, Śiva, the giver of boons, this mantra, namaḥ śivāya, is held to be the direct expressive name. ॥41॥
7.1.34.42: The seventy million great mantras, all the supreme ones together with the praṇava, dissolve into this very mantra and again come forth from it. ॥42॥
7.1.34.43: Those mantras become gracious and effective according to one's own eligibility and the like; but this one mantra alone, by the Lord's command, is open to all who are eligible. ॥43॥
7.1.34.44: Just as Śiva is able to protect all his own devotees, the lowly as well as the exalted, so too this mantra is able at all times. ॥44॥
7.1.34.45: And this mantra is indeed more powerful even than any other mantra; it alone is capable of protecting all, and no other is held to be so. ॥45॥
7.1.34.46: Therefore, giving up other mantras, be wholly devoted to the five-syllable mantra; when it rests on the tip of one's tongue, nothing here is difficult to attain. ॥46॥
7.1.34.47: And the Aghora weapon-mantra is the unsurpassed means of protection for Śaivas; considering that it too has arisen from that five-syllable mantra, be devoted to it, not otherwise. ॥47॥
7.1.34.48: This excellent ash was obtained by me from your father himself; it is perfected in the Virajā fire and wards off great calamities. ॥48॥
7.1.34.49: And take the mantra given to you by me, with my permission; by this alone, when repeated, protection will quickly be yours. ॥49॥
7.1.34.50: Vāyu said: Having thus instructed him and having said, may there be auspiciousness, the mother dismissed the young sage, who then placed her words on his head. ॥50॥
7.1.34.51: Having bowed to her and spoken thus, he set out to perform austerity; and then his mother said to him, may the gods bring you good fortune. ॥51॥
7.1.34.52: Permitted by her, he went to the Himālaya mountain and there, living on air and with concentrated mind, performed austerity hard to practise. ॥52॥
7.1.34.53: Having made a shrine with eight bricks and a liṅga of clay, and having invoked there Mahādeva, the imperishable, together with Ambā and his attendants, ॥53॥
7.1.34.54: and having worshipped him for a long time with devotion, with the five-syllable mantra alone, with leaves and flowers grown in the forest, he practised supreme austerity. ॥54॥
7.1.34.55: Then, as that boy Upamanyu, the best of brahmins, was practising austerity alone, emaciated, his mind attached to Śiva, ॥55॥
7.1.34.56: certain sages who had formerly been cursed by Marīci to become piśācas, tormenting him with demonic behaviour, created obstacles to his austerity. ॥56॥
7.1.34.57: And he, though being tormented by them, somehow continuing his austerity, kept crying out namaḥ śivāya like one in distress. ॥57॥
7.1.34.58: Merely on hearing that cry, those sages who had been obstructing his austerity let the boy go and attended upon him respectfully. ॥58॥
7.1.34.59: O sages, by the austerity of that great-souled brahmin Upamanyu, the whole world, moving and unmoving, became ablaze. ॥59॥
7.1.34.iti: Thus ends the thirty-fourth adhyāya, named The austerity of Upamanyu, in the Pūrva-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥34॥
7.1.35.1: Vāyu said: Then all those best of gods, their bodies blazing with the heat, quickly went to Vaikuṇṭha, and having bowed, they told Hari all of that. ॥1॥
7.1.35.2: Hearing their words then, the blessed Puruṣottama reflected, what is this, and he came to know its cause. ॥2॥
7.1.35.3: He went swiftly to Mandara, wishing to see Maheśvara. Seeing the god and bowing, he spoke thus with joined palms. ॥3॥
7.1.35.4: Viṣṇu said: O Lord, a certain brāhmaṇa known as Upamanyu has burned everything by his austerity for the sake of milk; restrain that. ॥4॥
7.1.35.5: Hearing these words of Viṣṇu, the god Maheśvara said: I shall restrain the child; so you go to your own abode. ॥5॥
7.1.35.6: Hearing Śambhu's words, that Viṣṇu, beloved of the gods, reassured all the immortals and the others and went to his own world. ॥6॥
7.1.35.7: Meanwhile the god, the Pināka-bearing supreme lord, assuming the form of Śakra, then resolved to go. ॥7॥
7.1.35.8: Then Sadāśiva, having himself assumed the body of the king of the immortals, went to the sage's penance-grove on a fine white elephant, together with gods, asuras, siddhas and great serpents. ॥8॥
7.1.35.9: That elephant then, gracefully fanning the lord with a divine yak-tail fan, held a white parasol with its left hand (trunk) over the king of the gods accompanied by Śacī. ॥9॥
7.1.35.10: The blessed Sadāśiva, accompanied by Umā, in the form of Śakra, shone with that parasol as Mount Mandara shines with the orb of the moon. ॥10॥
7.1.35.11: Having thus assumed the very form of Śakra, the supreme lord went to Upamanyu's hermitage to bestow grace. ॥11॥
7.1.35.12: Seeing that supreme lord Śiva bearing the form of Śakra, the best of great sages bowed with his head and himself spoke. ॥12॥
7.1.35.13: Upamanyu said: This hermitage of mine has been purified, O lord of gods, since you yourself have come, O lord of the world, blessed one, best of gods. ॥13॥
7.1.35.14: Vāyu said: Seeing the twice-born standing after speaking thus with hollowed palms joined, Hara, bearing the form of Śakra, spoke in a deep voice. ॥14॥
7.1.35.15: Śakra said: I am pleased with you by this austerity, O you of good vows; ask a boon. I will grant all you desire, O elder brother of Dhaumya, great sage. ॥15॥
7.1.35.16: Vāyu said: Addressed thus then by that Śakra, the foremost of sages, with joined palms, said: I choose devotion to Śiva. ॥16॥
7.1.35.17: Hearing that, Hari (Indra) said: Do you not know me, the protector of the gods, Śakra, sovereign of the three worlds, saluted by all the gods? ॥17॥
7.1.35.18: Be my devotee, O brahmin sage; worship me alone always. I will give you every good thing; and abandon Rudra, who is without qualities. ॥18॥
7.1.35.19: What purpose will you have with Rudra, who is without qualities, who is excluded from the row of gods and has become a piśāca? ॥19॥
7.1.35.20: Vāyu said: Hearing that, the sage, repeating the five-syllable mantra, and considering that he had come to create an obstacle to dharma, spoke to him. ॥20॥
7.1.35.21: Upamanyu said: All this has been said by you, intent on reviling Bhava; yet in passing you have indeed declared the great god's transcendence of the guṇas. ॥21॥
7.1.35.22: You indeed do not know Rudra, the lord of the lords of all gods, the progenitor of Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Maheśa, beyond Prakṛti. ॥22॥
7.1.35.23: Him whom the expounders of Brahman call being and non-being, manifest and unmanifest, eternal, one and many — from him therefore I choose a boon. ॥23॥
7.1.35.24: Him, the supreme, free from dialectical reasoning, granting the goal of Sāṅkhya and Yoga, whom the knowers of reality worship — from him therefore I choose a boon. ॥24॥
7.1.35.25: There is no reality higher than Śambhu, the cause of all causes, the creator of the gods Brahmā, Viṣṇu and the rest, the all-pervading one beyond the guṇas. ॥25॥
7.1.35.26: What use is saying much here? I infer today that a great sin was committed by me in another birth, since I have heard the reviling of Bhava. ॥26॥
7.1.35.27: Having heard the reviling of Bhava, one should at that very moment give up one's own body; having swiftly slain that reviler, he goes to Śiva's world. ॥27॥
7.1.35.28: Let this desire of mine for milk stand aside for now, O vilest of gods; having slain you with Śiva's weapon, I shall abandon this body. ॥28॥
7.1.35.29: Vāyu said: Having said this to him, Upamanyu, resolved himself to die, abandoning even his longing for milk, prepared to slay Śakra. ॥29॥
7.1.35.30: Then, taking dreadful ash consecrated with the Aghora weapon-mantra and hurling it at Śakra, the sage roared aloud. ॥30॥
7.1.35.31: Remembering Śambhu's pair of feet, Upamanyu, ready to burn his own body, stood holding the fiery concentration (āgneyī dhāraṇā). ॥31॥
7.1.35.32: When the brahmin had thus resolved, the blessed destroyer of Bhaga's eyes checked that yogin's concentration by a gentle counter-concentration. ॥32॥
7.1.35.33: That Aghora weapon he had released and hurled, Nandin, dear to Śaṅkara, caught in mid-course at the command of the Lord of Nandin. ॥33॥
7.1.35.34: The blessed supreme lord, assuming his own form, showed the brahmin his form crested with the crescent moon. ॥34॥
7.1.35.35: A thousand oceans of milk, and an ocean of nectar, and oceans of curd and the like, and an ocean of ghee, ॥35॥
7.1.35.36: an ocean of fruits, likewise an ocean of foods to chew and to eat, and a mountain of cakes — these the lord showed to the boy. ॥36॥
7.1.35.37: Thus the god was seen with the Goddess upon the bull, surrounded by the lords of the gaṇas and by divine weapons such as the trident. ॥37॥
7.1.35.38: Drums resounded in the sky and a shower of flowers fell; the ten directions were filled with gods headed by Viṣṇu, Brahmā and Indra. ॥38॥
7.1.35.39: Then Upamanyu, engulfed by the waves of an ocean of bliss, fell to the ground like a staff, with a mind bowed in devotion. ॥39॥
7.1.35.40: At that moment there, the blessed Bhava, smiling, called him, come, come, and, smelling (kissing) his head, granted him boons. ॥40॥
7.1.35.41: Śiva said: Enjoy with your kinsmen, always and as much as you wish, foods to be chewed and foods to be eaten. Be ever happy, free from sorrow, and devoted to me. ॥41॥
7.1.35.42: O Upamanyu, most fortunate one, this Pārvatī is indeed your mother. I have made you my son today, and the ocean of milk has been given to you. ॥42॥
7.1.35.43: And an ocean of honey, an ocean of curd and rice, an ocean of ghee and cooked rice, and an ocean of fruits and the like — ॥43॥
7.1.35.44: and mountains of cakes, and likewise an ocean of foods to be chewed and eaten — these have been given to you by me; accept them, O great sage. ॥44॥
7.1.35.45: Your father is Mahādeva and your mother is indeed Jagadambikā, the Mother of the world. Immortality has been granted by me, and the eternal leadership of the gaṇas. ॥45॥
7.1.35.46: Choose, with great joy, other excellent boons desired by your mind; being pleased, I shall grant them — there need be no hesitation about this. ॥46॥
7.1.35.47: Vāyu said: Having spoken thus, Mahādeva took him up with both hands, smelled (kissed) his head, and presented him to the Goddess, saying, this is your son. ॥47॥
7.1.35.48: And the Goddess, with affection as for Guha, placed her lotus-hand on his head and bestowed on him the imperishable status of Kumāra. ॥48॥
7.1.35.49: The Ocean of Milk too, taking bodily form and holding sweet milk in his hand, approached and gave him imperishable milk solidified into a mass. ॥49॥
7.1.35.50: With a fully satisfied mind, Śiva gave him yogic sovereignty, constant contentment, imperishable knowledge of Brahman, and supreme prosperity. ॥50॥
7.1.35.51: Then Śambhu, pleased at heart, seeing the splendour of his austerity, again gave a divine boon to the sage Upamanyu. ॥51॥
7.1.35.52: He gave him the Pāśupata vow, knowledge, and the discipline of the vow in its true essence, as well as supreme and lasting skill in exposition. ॥52॥
7.1.35.53: He too, having obtained divine boons and perpetual youthfulness from that Śiva and from that Śivā, became joyful. ॥53॥
7.1.35.54: Then, with a delighted heart, bowing low with joined palms, that brahmin begged a boon from Maheśvara, the God of gods. ॥54॥
7.1.35.55: Upamanyu said: Be gracious, O Lord of the god of gods; be gracious, O Supreme Lord. Grant me supreme, divine, unwavering devotion to you. ॥55॥
7.1.35.56: O Mahādeva, grant me always faith in those connected with you, and servitude to you, supreme love, and your presence at all times. ॥56॥
7.1.35.57: Having thus spoken, Upamanyu, the best of brahmins, pleased at heart, praised Mahādeva in a voice choked with joy. ॥57॥
7.1.35.58: O God of gods, O Mahādeva, loving to those who take refuge in you, be gracious always, O ocean of compassion, O Śaṅkara together with Ambā. ॥58॥
7.1.35.59: Vāyu said: Thus addressed, Mahādeva, the giver of boons to all, pleased at heart, replied to Upamanyu, the best of sages. ॥59॥
7.1.35.60: Śiva said: Dear Upamanyu, I am pleased; everything has been granted to you by me. You are a firm devotee, O brahmin sage; you were only being tested by me. ॥60॥
7.1.35.61: Be free from old age and death, free from sorrow, renowned, endowed with radiance, and possessed of divine knowledge. ॥61॥
7.1.35.62: Your kinsmen, family and lineage shall always be imperishable, O best of brahmins, and your devotion to me eternal. ॥62॥
7.1.35.63: And I shall always be present in your hermitage, O best of brahmins; you shall indeed roam joyfully near me. ॥63॥
7.1.35.64: Having spoken thus and granted the boons, the blessed Lord Īśāna, Hara, whose radiance equals ten million suns, vanished right there. ॥64॥
7.1.35.65: Upamanyu, pleased at heart, having obtained the boons from that boon-giver, went to his mother's dwelling and attained surpassing happiness. ॥65॥
7.1.35.iti: Thus ends the thirty-fifth adhyāya, named The life of Upamanyu, in the Pūrva-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, contained in the saṃhitā of twenty-four thousand verses composed by Vyāsa, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥35॥
